map.subsystem: Medtronic MiniMed 680G/770G/780G read-only BLE driver (plugins/shipped/medtronic) — phone-as-peripheral connection + SAKE session + CGM/IDD/history read layer + plugin capability surface, plus the tools/medtronic-ble-spike offline de-risk harness and the user pairing doc.

capabilities.name: Inverted BLE topology: phone is the peripheral, pump is the central
capabilities.behavior: Unlike Tandem (phone = GATT client/central), the MiniMed 700-series pump is the BLE central. The phone advertises as a connectable peripheral named "Mobile 000001" and stands up a GATT server; the pump scans, finds it, connects, and drives the SAKE handshake. There is no active scan and no device address to dial: DevicePlugin.connect(address, config) ignores `address` entirely. Pairing style is PairingStyle.ADVERTISE_AND_WAIT with advertisedName = "Mobile 000001". After SAKE completes, the phone opens a second GATT *client* connection back to the same BluetoothDevice (captured from the server callback) to read the pump's CGM/IDD/Battery/DIS services — it must never start a fresh scan/advertise cycle for that.
edge_cases: Emulators and some chipsets cannot advertise as a BLE peripheral at all: isSupported() = adapter != null && isEnabled && isMultipleAdvertisementSupported && bluetoothLeAdvertiser != null. Failure surfaces as PERIPHERAL_UNSUPPORTED and the flow can never pair.
A pump connecting during scan(), CONNECTING or RECONNECTING all collapse into ConnectionState.CONNECTING; other states ignore the event.

capabilities.name: Advertising contract (what the pump scans for)
capabilities.behavior: AdvertiseSettings: connectable=true, timeout=0 (advertise until stopped), txPower = ADVERTISE_TX_POWER_MEDIUM. Mode is ADVERTISE_MODE_LOW_LATENCY for RECONNECT (paired pumps scan infrequently and miss long intervals) and ADVERTISE_MODE_BALANCED for FIRST_PAIR. AdvertiseData carries manufacturer data under company ID 0x01F9 with payload `0x00 || ASCII(localName) || 0x00`, plus the service UUID (SIG-based 0xFE82 first-pair / 0xFE81 reconnect), setIncludeDeviceName(false) (GAP name intentionally omitted to stay inside the 31-byte budget) and setIncludeTxPowerLevel(true). The pump only connects to advertisers whose name matches Regex("Mobile .{0,7}"); LOCAL_NAME_PREFIX = "Mobile ". BLE pairing security is Just Works, IO capability NoInputNoOutput (io-cap 3); the pump requests MITM but has no LE Secure Connections, so the stack falls back to Just Works. App-layer auth is SAKE, not BLE pairing.
edge_cases: DEFAULT_LOCAL_NAME is a hard-coded "Mobile 000001" for every install (TODO: per-install identity).
advertisingModeFor(paired, forceFirstPair) = RECONNECT only when paired && !forceFirstPair; everything else FIRST_PAIR.
startAdvertising SecurityException or a null BluetoothLeAdvertiser reports synthetic error code -1 (ADVERTISER_UNAVAILABLE); a failed GATT-server open reports -2 (GATT_SERVER_UNAVAILABLE).

capabilities.name: UUID base scheme: SIG base vs Medtronic vendor base (issue #844 fix)
capabilities.behavior: Two 128-bit expansions of 16-bit short codes. SIG base: 0000XXXX-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb. Medtronic vendor base: 0000XXXX-0000-1000-0000-009132591325 — note the variant field is 0000, NOT the SIG 8000. Getting this wrong silently broke pairing and every IDD/HAT/CM read. Split today: SAKE *service* is advertised/registered on the SIG base (0xFE82), but the SAKE *characteristic* the pump subscribes to is the vendor-base 0xFE82. The phone's Device Information container is the vendor 0x0900 service (not SIG 0x180A), even though the characteristics inside it are standard SIG DIS UUIDs; a pump only sees 0x180A and refuses to pair. Pump-side IDD (0x100), HAT (0x300), CM (0x600) are vendor base; CGM (0x181F), Battery (0x180F), RACP (0x2A52), CCCD (0x2902) are SIG.
edge_cases: 0x0900 is discovered, never advertised.
The read layer addresses the pump's DIS by characteristic UUID, not service UUID, so it works against the pump's own 0x180A.

capabilities.name: Full GATT UUID inventory
capabilities.behavior: Advertised/SAKE: SAKE_SERVICE_FIRST_PAIR_16 = 0xFE82, SAKE_SERVICE_RECONNECT_16 = 0xFE81 (both SIG-based), SAKE_CHARACTERISTIC = vendor 0xFE82 (NOTIFY + WRITE, PERMISSION_WRITE, with a CCCD). Phone-exposed DIS container = vendor 0x0900 holding SIG 0x2A29 manufacturer, 0x2A24 model, 0x2A25 serial, 0x2A26 firmware, 0x2A27 hardware, 0x2A28 software, 0x2A23 systemId, 0x2A50 PnP ID, 0x2A2A regulatory cert (empty). Pump-side: Battery service 0x180F / level 0x2A19; CGM service 0x181F with measurement 0x2AA7, feature 0x2AA8, SOCP 0x2AAC; IDD vendor 0x100 with status 0x102, features 0x104, SRCP 0x105, history data 0x108; HAT vendor 0x300 (slice 0x350, RTMCP 0x360, RMCPSE 0x370) — present but deliberately unused; CM vendor 0x600 (0x601/0x602) unused. RACP 0x2A52 is shared by CGM, IDD and HAT. CCCD 0x2902.
edge_cases: HAT is explicitly not used: upstream hats.py returns "Not Supported"/"No Records Found" for every request, so history goes over the IDD RACP instead.
CM (certificate management) is not needed for read-only.

capabilities.name: Phone-side GATT server registration order and placeholder DIS values
capabilities.behavior: openGattServer() populates a ConcurrentLinkedQueue with [DeviceInfoService, SakeService] and adds them one at a time: addService -> onServiceAdded -> addNextService, because the Android GATT server accepts only one add in flight. Advertising is deferred (pendingAdvertise) until the last service is registered, so a fast pump cannot discover an empty GATT table. A failed onServiceAdded status calls failPendingAdvertise() -> onAdvertiseFailed(-2) — this is the one BLE step with no timeout, so without it the manager would hang in CONNECTING forever. DIS placeholder values: manufacturer "GlycemicGPT", model "Mobile", serial = the advertised local name, hardware/firmware/software "0", systemId = 8 zero bytes, PnP ID = 7 zero bytes, regulatory cert = empty. The characteristic *set* mirrors JavaPumpConnector so a pump enumerating DIS membership sees the same table.
edge_cases: Open TODO(48.A2): confirm a real pump does not validate any DIS field value (JavaPumpConnector spoofs a realistic app-version string).

onDescriptorReadRequest is deliberately ungated and answers ANY descriptor read with its stored value (default 0x0000), because Android peripherals get no auto-response and an unanswered read stalls the pump (issue #844).
onCharacteristic/DescriptorReadRequest honor the ATT offset; offset < 0 or > size responds GATT_INVALID_OFFSET.

capabilities.name: SAKE CCCD subscribe/unsubscribe detection on the phone's GATT server
capabilities.behavior: onDescriptorWriteRequest gates on descriptor.uuid == CCCD && descriptor.characteristic.uuid == SAKE_CHARACTERISTIC && value.size >= 2. If (value[0] & 0x01) != 0 -> onSakeSubscribed() (this is the cue to emit the wake-up frame). If value[0]==0 && value[1]==0 -> onSakeUnsubscribed(). Anything else is logged and ignored. The descriptor's stored value is then updated and, if responseNeeded, GATT_SUCCESS is returned with the written value echoed. onCharacteristicWriteRequest forwards any write on the SAKE characteristic verbatim to onSakeWrite(value) and responds GATT_SUCCESS when responseNeeded. onMtuChanged is observational only — the driver never requests an MTU and keeps its own PDUs <= 20 bytes regardless of what the central negotiates.
edge_cases: Indication-enable (0x02) also satisfies the `& 0x01`? No — 0x02 & 0x01 == 0 and 0x02/0x00 is not the disable pattern, so it falls to the "unexpected, ignoring" branch.

capabilities.name: Connection state machine
capabilities.behavior: States (shared ConnectionState enum): DISCONNECTED, SCANNING, CONNECTING, AUTHENTICATING, AUTH_FAILED, CONNECTED, RECONNECTING. Transitions: startSession() -> CONNECTING (advertise FIRST_PAIR or RECONNECT); reconnectIfPaired() -> CONNECTING (RECONNECT, no-op if unpaired); scan() -> SCANNING (FIRST_PAIR, autoReconnect=false). Pump connects to the GATT server -> cancel pairing-wait timer, clear fault, record address, stopAdvertising() (single-peer), SCANNING|CONNECTING|RECONNECTING -> CONNECTING, emit DiscoveredDevice. Pump subscribes to SAKE -> AUTHENTICATING + arm auth timeout + driver.onSubscribed(). Handshake completes -> cancel timeout, store sakeSession, savePairing(address, localName), CONNECTED. Handshake fails or times out -> AUTH_FAILED (latched), autoReconnect=false, stopAdvertising(). Disconnect while AUTH_FAILED -> stays AUTH_FAILED, stopAdvertising(), no reconnect. Disconnect otherwise: if autoReconnect && isPaired -> RECONNECTING + re-advertise RECONNECT; else teardown -> DISCONNECTED.
edge_cases: Every public entry point and every BLE callback hops onto the SerialWorker before touching lifecycle state; fields stay @Volatile so UI/read layer observe latest values without locking.
AUTH_FAILED is deliberately sticky so the inevitable pump disconnect does not reset it or start a reconnect loop against a pump that just rejected us.
close() tears down synchronously on the caller thread (a posted teardown could be dropped as the worker stops), then worker.stop() + scope.cancel(); the manager is unusable afterwards.

capabilities.name: Connection faults and their timers
capabilities.behavior: MedtronicConnectionFault enum, exposed as a StateFlow<MedtronicConnectionFault?> alongside connectionState because several faults produce no state transition: PERIPHERAL_UNSUPPORTED, ADVERTISE_FAILED, HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT, AUTH_FAILED, BOUND_ELSEWHERE_SUSPECTED. Timers: DEFAULT_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000 (SAKE is six round trips of 20-byte frames), armed on AUTHENTICATING; on expiry, if still AUTHENTICATING -> HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT + AUTH_FAILED + autoReconnect=false + stopAdvertising. DEFAULT_PAIRING_WAIT_MS = 60_000, armed only for FIRST_PAIR advertising; on expiry, if state is CONNECTING or SCANNING -> BOUND_ELSEWHERE_SUSPECTED (the pump is probably still bound to another phone). RECONNECT advertising waits indefinitely (the paired pump scans infrequently). Both timers run on the manager's coroutine scope but re-check state on the worker thread so they cannot flip an already-CONNECTED session. Mapped 1:1 to the platform PairingFault enum for the UI.
edge_cases: BOUND_ELSEWHERE_SUSPECTED is an explicitly-labelled working assumption from desk research; TODO(48.A2) to tune/confirm the 60s window against a real pump.
PERIPHERAL_UNSUPPORTED and BOUND_ELSEWHERE produce NO ConnectionState change — the fault flow is the only signal.

capabilities.name: Pairing persistence, auto-reconnect and unpair
capabilities.behavior: Pairing is persisted via the shared PumpCredentialProvider: on handshake completion, credentialStore.savePairing(connectedAddress, localName). SAKE has no pairing code (authentication is the static-key handshake plus the OS BLE bond), so the credential "code" slot records the advertised identity string instead. isPaired() gates reconnectIfPaired() and the auto-reconnect branch. disconnect() sets autoReconnect=false and tears down advertising + session but KEEPS the pairing. unpair() reads getPairedAddress() ?: connectedAddress, tears down, clearPairing(), then removeBond(address) — implemented by reflection on the hidden BluetoothDevice.removeBond() and returning false if not BOND_BONDED. The plugin wires onActivated() -> reconnectIfPaired(), onDeactivated() -> disconnect(), shutdown() -> close().
edge_cases: The JPAKE credential slots on PumpCredentialProvider are Tandem-only and unused here.
MAC addresses are logged at DEBUG only; WARN+ is Sentry-eligible and must not carry a device identifier.

capabilities.name: Discovery is advertise-and-wait, not a scan
capabilities.behavior: scan() returns a callbackFlow. If !peripheral.isSupported() it logs WARN, posts PERIPHERAL_UNSUPPORTED and closes the flow immediately. Otherwise it installs an onDiscovered trySend hook, sets autoReconnect=false and begins FIRST_PAIR advertising in state SCANNING. When a pump connects to the GATT server it emits DiscoveredDevice(name = localName, address = pump MAC, pluginId = "com.glycemicgpt.medtronic") — note the emitted name is the PHONE's advertised name, not a pump name. awaitClose clears the hook and, only if state is still SCANNING (i.e. no pump connected), tears down; once a pump is connecting/authenticating the session owns the lifecycle. Unlike a central scan, a discovered pump cannot be "connected to later" — the connection it initiated proceeds straight into SAKE.
edge_cases: PLUGIN_ID = "com.glycemicgpt.medtronic" is the single source of truth, re-exported by MedtronicDevicePlugin.PLUGIN_ID and PluginMetadata.id.

capabilities.name: SAKE handshake wire choreography (SakeHandshakeDriver)
capabilities.behavior: State on the worker thread: session, pumpSubscribed, complete, failed. onSubscribed(): if already pumpSubscribed, no-op; if !complete && session.stage != 0, rebuild the session ("pump resubscribed mid-handshake; restarting SAKE state"); set pumpSubscribed, emit the 20-byte all-zero wake-up notification. onUnsubscribed(): clear pumpSubscribed so a later subscribe restarts cleanly. onPumpWrite(value): copies the array, posts to the worker; if complete||failed it is ignored (post-handshake traffic belongs to the read layer); otherwise session.onPumpWrite(copy) -> non-null response is notified back, null means handshake complete -> complete=true, listener.onAuthenticated(session). Any exception latches failed=true and fires listener.onAuthFailed(e) exactly once. reset() re-arms a fresh session and clears all flags. All notifications go through PduFramer.fragment (SAKE frames are exactly 20 bytes so it is a single PDU) and a failed notifySink is logged at WARN.
edge_cases: The wake-up frame is NOT part of the handshake state machine — feeding it into onPumpWrite would advance the machine with the wrong input.
The pump's FIRST write is 20 zero bytes and produces msg0.
Failure is latched so a corrupted session cannot fire onAuthFailed repeatedly.

capabilities.name: MedtronicSakeSession: JavaSake wrapper and session keying model
capabilities.behavior: Wraps org.openminimed.sake.SakeServer(keyDb, DeviceType.MOBILE_APPLICATION, rng) — the phone is the SAKE *server*, the pump is the SAKE *client* (DeviceType.INSULIN_PUMP). Default keyDb is Constants.KEYDB_PUMP_EXTRACTED (firmware-extracted static key database shipped inside the JavaSake artifact); default RNG is SecureRandomRngSource. Stages advance 0 -> 1 -> 3 -> 5 -> 6; HANDSHAKE_COMPLETE_STAGE = 6, isComplete == (stage == 6). newWakeUpFrame() = ByteArray(Session.MESSAGE_SIZE) (20 zero bytes, fresh allocation each call). onPumpWrite() throws MacFailureException on CMAC/permit verification failure. Post-handshake: encryptForPump() uses server.session().serverCrypt().encrypt (phone -> pump), decryptFromPump() uses clientCrypt().decrypt (pump -> phone) — mirroring JavaSake's own handshake5C which decrypts the pump's stage-5 permit with clientCrypt; its rx_seq ends at 2, aligned with the pump's clientCrypt tx_seq. Not thread-safe: drive from one worker thread only.
edge_cases: encrypt/decrypt throw IllegalStateException if called before stage 6.
The cipher direction mapping is flagged for live re-confirmation (48.A2) — there is a CipherDirectionConfirmationTest.

Decrypting advances the inbound sequence counter, so encrypted static reads must be ordered against the other reads on the same session; a late/duplicate notification after an exchange finishes would consume the next operation's sequence slot and desync the session (guarded by the `finished` flags).

capabilities.name: JavaSake / OpenMinimed dependency and pinned versions
capabilities.behavior: org.openminimed:javasake:0.2.0 from Maven Central (previously vendored under src/.../org/openminimed/sake/). Its only third-party runtime dep is BouncyCastle for AES-CMAC (the JDK/Android JCE has no CMAC); the driver explicitly pins org.bouncycastle:bcprov-jdk18on:1.84 over JavaSake's transitive 1.79 to clear a HIGH timing-channel advisory affecting >= 1.71, < 1.84. AES-CTR/ECB use the platform JCE. Both versions are locked in plugins/shipped/medtronic/gradle.lockfile and tools/medtronic-ble-spike/gradle.lockfile. Consumer ProGuard rules keep org.bouncycastle.crypto.macs.CMac, engines.AESEngine, params.KeyParameter and -dontwarn org.bouncycastle.**. Licensing: OpenMinimed is GPL-3.0, used with explicit permission of palmarci (Pál Marci); GlycemicGPT is GPL-3.0, so copyleft propagation is a non-issue. Every ported file cites its upstream source file.
edge_cases: Four upstream repos feed the driver: PythonSake (SAKE reference), PythonPumpConnector (reader logic, ported line-for-line to Kotlin), JavaSake (runtime dependency), JavaPumpConnector (BLE peripheral scaffolding, informed structure only).
Renovate tracks javasake as a Tier D (crypto) dependency requiring manual review.
Module targets: compileSdk 35, minSdk 30, Java 17.

capabilities.name: AesEcb Semgrep exclusion (documented security decision)
capabilities.behavior: The security-scan workflow runs Semgrep 1.169.0 (pip-pinned) with rulesets p/kotlin, p/java, p/secrets over app/, wear-device/, watchface/, plugins/, tools/, and passes `--exclude 'AesEcb.java' --exclude '.gradle'`. Stated reason: AesEcb.java is vendored from OpenMinimed JavaSake and is re-vendored (not patched) on upstream bumps (#695/#696), so its intentional legacy AES/ECB usage must never fail the gate. Because JavaSake is now consumed as the Maven artifact with no vendored source in-tree, the exclusion is documented as INERT today and retained only for the re-vendor case. Gate policy: fail on HIGH/ERROR-severity findings only; WARNING/INFO are printed but do not block; a crashed scanner fails closed. Note the rule packs are fetched from the registry at scan time, so rule content can move between runs even with the CLI pinned.
edge_cases: Documented revisit trigger for the broader SAST posture: add an APK/manifest SAST gate if the app is ever distributed via the Play Store, or if ANY write/therapeutic surface (bolus, basal, pump-setting, device-command) is introduced.
tools/medtronic-ble-spike is deliberately inside Semgrep scope but outside the plugins/shipped/**/ble/** BLE-review path rules.

capabilities.name: Static SAKE key-database posture
capabilities.behavior: org.openminimed.sake.Constants (inside the JavaSake artifact) and the spike's SakeTestVectors embed firmware-extracted SAKE key databases and a captured 780G pairing trace. Documented posture for security review: these are SHARED SAKE protocol constants — the same values live inside every 700-series pump and authenticate any phone that pairs with it. They are not session secrets, not unique per device, and not credentials. They already ship publicly in OpenMinimed's GPL-3.0 repository and artifact, so using them introduces no new secret. The CUSTOM_* databases are synthetic generated test keys. Any scanner flag on these values is to be treated as a known, published-upstream artifact, not a leak. The driver selects Constants.KEYDB_PUMP_EXTRACTED as the default KeyDatabase; the manager accepts an injectable keyDatabase parameter for tests.

capabilities.name: SerialWorker: single-thread serialization discipline
capabilities.behavior: Interface SerialWorker { post(task); stop() } guarantees tasks never run concurrently and preserve submission order, so the not-thread-safe MedtronicSakeSession needs no locking. Production impl HandlerThreadSerialWorker wraps an Android HandlerThread (name "medtronic-sake"), started eagerly and reused across connect/disconnect cycles; stop() sets a volatile stopped flag, removes all callbacks and quitSafely()s — post() is a no-op afterwards. The same single worker instance is shared by the connection manager, the handshake driver AND the GATT-client transport (AndroidMedtronicGattLink hops inbound notification PDUs onto it), so every onPdu callback across every subscribed characteristic is delivered serialized on one thread — the explicit threading contract MedtronicSessionReader relies on to keep its per-exchange state lock-free. Rationale: blocking the binder thread that delivers GATT callbacks stalls the whole Bluetooth stack.
edge_cases: A reader calls unsubscribe from inside its onPdu handler (on the worker thread), so the blocking CCCD round trip is deliberately deferred off that thread onto the watchdog executor — otherwise it would stall connection-lifecycle events.

capabilities.name: MTU policy and PDU framing
capabilities.behavior: PduFramer: DEFAULT_MTU = 23, ATT_HEADER_SIZE = 3, MAX_PDU_SIZE = 20. The driver NEVER calls requestMtu() in either direction (peripheral or client). fragment(payload, maxPduSize = 20) requires maxPduSize in 1..20; a payload that already fits returns one chunk (a copy); an empty payload yields a single empty chunk so the boundary is still transmitted. reassemble(list) is the exact inverse. Inbound is looser: the ATT MTU is per-bearer and the pump raises it from its own side (it advertises MTU 184), so pump-to-phone notifications can exceed 20 bytes — live multi-PDU history reads (PR #852) arrive as per-PDU SAKE ciphertext whose 20-byte plaintext fragments imply 23-byte on-wire notifications. Inbound reassembly lives above the transport seam in NotificationReassembler.
edge_cases: SAKE handshake messages are already exactly 20 bytes and pass through unfragmented; the framer is the single MTU choke point.

capabilities.name: AndroidMedtronicGattLink: GATT-client transport, serialization and timeouts
capabilities.behavior: Implements MedtronicGattLink over a BluetoothGatt client to the pump's own GATT server, using the BluetoothDevice captured by the peripheral. Every read/write/subscribe/unsubscribe and the watchdog cleanup runs under a single ReentrantLock (opLock) and BLOCKS the calling thread until the matching GATT callback fires, bounded by operationTimeoutMs. DEFAULT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000; DEFAULT_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000; subscriptionTimeoutMs defaults to MedtronicReadGateway.DEFAULT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000. Connect is lazy on first use: device.connectGatt(ctx, autoConnect=false, cb, TRANSPORT_LE) -> on STATE_CONNECTED go straight to discoverServices() (never requestMtu) -> onServicesDiscovered completes the connect slot. Only after success are `gatt`, connectedAddress and the service index published. Reused until disconnect. CCCD payloads are literal byte arrays: enable-notification 0x01 0x00, enable-indication 0x02 0x00, disable 0x00 0x00.
edge_cases: Stale-completion safety: an operation timeout tears the client GATT down (closeGatt); every operational callback rejects any BluetoothGatt that is not the current `gatt`, so a late completion lands on a discarded handle and can never satisfy a later op's slot. Connect-phase callbacks are additionally identity-checked against `connectingGatt`.
Synthetic statuses: -1 LOCAL_TIMEOUT, -2 LOCAL_REJECTED. gattStatusName maps 0x02/0x03/0x05/0x06/0x07/0x08/0x0D/0x13/0x16/0x22/0x3E/0x85 to names for WARN logs.
API 33+ uses the new writeCharacteristic/writeDescriptor returning BluetoothStatusCodes.SUCCESS; below that the deprecated setValue+write path.
Subscribe chooses indication vs notification from PROPERTY_INDICATE on the characteristic.

capabilities.name: Read-only enforcement in the transport (defense in depth)
capabilities.behavior: MedtronicGattLink.write() checks the characteristic against a hard allow-list WRITABLE_CONTROL_POINTS = { RACP 0x2A52, CGM SOCP 0x2AAC, IDD SRCP vendor 0x105 }. Anything else is refused with a WARN ("characteristic is not a permitted control point") and the write silently returns — so a buggy caller can never issue a therapeutic write opcode. Beyond that, only static reads and CCCD descriptor writes are ever issued. A failed control-point write is best-effort: it removes the handler and degrades to the gateway's operation timeout (the pump simply never responds) rather than escaping the readers' Result<T> contract. At the plugin layer the driver declares only GLUCOSE_SOURCE, INSULIN_SOURCE, PUMP_STATUS — there is no PUMP_CONTROL capability in the platform and no method writes to the pump. HistoryReader issues only RACP report/count opcodes, never delete/abort.
edge_cases: Only GET-class SOCP/SRCP opcodes are allowed by convention in MedtronicSessionReader — no calibration or control opcode is constructed anywhere.
MedtronicHistoryParser parses records only; it never constructs a write/control message.

capabilities.name: Shared RACP characteristic service-scoping
capabilities.behavior: The SIG 0x2A52 RACP characteristic exists under BOTH the CGM and IDD services on the pump, so a bare-UUID lookup is ambiguous and picking wrong silently reads the wrong log. buildServiceIndex maps bare characteristic UUID -> list of (serviceUuid, characteristic) and computes racpServiceUuids = the set of services exposing RACP. resolve(): 0 candidates -> throw; 1 candidate -> use it and, only if its service is in racpServiceUuids, record lastResolvedServiceUuid (so a Battery/Device-Info read can never poison scoping); >1 candidates -> resolveAmbiguous, which prefers the candidate whose service == lastResolvedServiceUuid, then falls back to a service with a live subscription, and otherwise THROWS rather than guessing. This works because each reader resolves that exchange's data characteristic (CGM Measurement 0x2AA7 or IDD History Data 0x108) immediately before touching the control point. Preferring the resolved context over live subscriptions stops a dangling handler from a failed prior exchange hijacking the scope.
edge_cases: The deferred CCCD-disable path compares the *resolved characteristic identity*, not the bare UUID, so a new subscription on the other service's RACP does not shield this one's CCCD from being disabled.

capabilities.name: Dangling-subscription watchdog and cancellation cleanup
capabilities.behavior: A reader only unsubscribes when the pump responds, so a gateway timeout that cancels the driving coroutine would leave dangling subscriptions that desync the next exchange. Two mechanisms: (1) SubscriptionWatchdog (production: a single daemon ScheduledExecutorService thread "medtronic-gatt-watchdog") is armed for subscriptionTimeoutMs (30_000) whenever a subscription registration is still current after its CCCD ack; on fire it drops all handlers lock-free, then disables each CCCD under opLock. (2) MedtronicGattLink.cancelAllSubscriptions() is invoked from the gateway's cont.invokeOnCancellation: it clears handlers immediately (the no-dangling-notification guarantee) and DEFERS the blocking CCCD disables onto the watchdog executor, because the cancellation handler may run on kotlinx's process-global timeout thread where blocking would stall every delay/withTimeout in the app. unsubscribe() follows the same discipline (drop handler first, defer the disable).
edge_cases: disableNotifications skips if the owning BluetoothGatt was replaced by a reconnect, and skips if the same resolved characteristic has been re-subscribed by a newer exchange (which would otherwise silently starve that read).
Arming the watchdog is guarded by an identity check (handlers[uuid] === sub) because cancelAllSubscriptions runs lock-free and could clear the registration while the CCCD ack is in flight.

capabilities.name: NotificationReassembler and the exact-multiple ambiguity
capabilities.behavior: Each inbound notification PDU is individually SAKE-encrypted, so the reassembler is fed decrypted PLAINTEXT fragments. Rule: full fragments until a short one ends the frame — a fragment smaller than maxPduSize (20) completes the frame; an empty PDU is ignored (a real encrypted frame is never empty and must not falsely terminate). MAX_FRAME_SIZE = 512; exceeding it resets and throws MedtronicReadException, capping the memory a malfunctioning or hostile peer can force. hasPartialFrame() / fragmentCount() / flush() / reset() expose the pending state. The documented ambiguity: a frame whose plaintext length is an exact multiple of 20 never gets a short terminator. For the FINAL record of an exchange the pending fragments can be flushed as one last frame — live 780G reads hit this on real records. An INTERMEDIATE exact-multiple record still merges silently with its successor; pinning exact on-wire fragment sizes is TODO(48.A2).
edge_cases: Flushed bytes are transport-indistinguishable from a record truncated mid-stream, so callers MUST validate before accepting (HistoryReader does; the CGM path relies on its own parse + the fact that no cursor advances).

capabilities.name: MedtronicSessionReader: the six control-point exchange patterns
capabilities.behavior: (1) reportLastRecord(dataChar, controlPoint): subscribe both, write plaintext RACP_REPORT_LAST_RECORD = [0x01,0x06] (Report Stored Records / Last Record), decrypt each measurement PDU, reassemble; terminate when the plaintext indication equals RACP_REPORT_SUCCESS = [0x06,0x00,0x01,0x01]; anything else fails. (2) socpGet: appends a little-endian E2E-CRC to the request, SAKE-encrypts it, writes it, and returns the first reassembled decrypted response. (3) srcpGet: same but with NO E2E-CRC wrapper (the 780G does not enable E2E in the IDD service; TODO(48.A2) to honor the features flag per model). (4) decryptedRead(uuid): synchronous plain GATT read then clientCrypt decrypt, for the encrypted static IDD Status/Features characteristics. (5) reportRecords: multi-record streaming with caller-supplied isSuccess and validateRecoveredFrame predicates; MAX_RECORDS_PER_REPORT = 50_000. (6) controlPointQuery: write, deliver the first indication verbatim (used for record-count). All exchanges unsubscribe both characteristics on finish and are idempotent via a `finished` flag. The framework carries NO timers by design — the caller must bound every exchange.
edge_cases: CGM report-last recovery: RACP success + pending fragments + no record -> flush and deliver (safe, no cursor advances, a bad parse just retries next poll). RACP success + a complete record AND pending fragments -> FAIL (report-last returns exactly one record). RACP success + no record at all -> FAIL.

IDD reportRecords: success + pending fragments -> flush, then validateRecoveredFrame decides; rejection FAILS the exchange loudly so cursors stay put (accepting a truncated record would let history cursors advance past a record the pump sent = permanent skip). The default validator rejects.
Any decrypt/MAC/length exception inside a notification handler is converted to Result.failure rather than escaping the delivery thread and hanging the exchange.

capabilities.name: MedtronicReadGateway: single-flight, timeouts and history paging
capabilities.behavior: Bundles all reads behind suspend Result<T>. Two mutexes: readMutex (fair/FIFO) serializes EVERY exchange into single-flight because the link is strictly one-exchange-at-a-time with no transaction id, and the polling orchestrator drives tiers as independent coroutines; historyMutex additionally serializes whole getHistoryLogs walks so two callers cannot interleave paging loops. DEFAULT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000 wraps every read via withTimeout; expiry becomes Result.failure(MedtronicReadException). sessionRead resolves link + session BEFORE queueing (so "not connected" fails fast instead of blocking), registers cont.invokeOnCancellation { link.cancelAllSubscriptions() }, and runs on ioDispatcher. blockingRead uses runInterruptible so a timeout becomes a thread interrupt (a blocking GATT read is not a suspension point). History paging: read last record; if null or lastSeq <= sinceSequence return empty; then walk newest-first in HISTORY_BATCH_SIZE = 200 sequence windows, lowSeq = max(sinceSequence+1, highSeq-199), each page its own sessionRead/timeout, highSeq = lowSeq-1 after each page.
edge_cases: The walk is driven by the REQUESTED window, never by page content: a page routinely parses smaller than its window, and ending on content would let cursor-advancing callers skip older records permanently.
An EMPTY page ends the walk (the pump purges oldest-first, so retained sequences are contiguous).
A failed page fails the WHOLE call — returning partial newer pages would advance callers' cursors past the un-fetched older window.
maxTotalHistoryRecords defaults to 50_000 across all pages; exceeding it fails loudly with cursors unchanged.
readMutex is released between pages so a CGM/keep-alive read can interleave with a long backfill.
WARN logs deliberately carry only op + exception class name — reader failure messages embed health values (SG, IOB, basal, reservoir) and raw pump bytes, and WARN is forwarded to Sentry.

capabilities.name: CgmReader: sensor glucose read path and safety gating
capabilities.behavior: readLatest(): plain-read CGM Feature 0x2AA8, parse it for the E2E-CRC bit (per pump, never hard-coded for 780G as upstream does), then reportLastRecord over CGM Measurement 0x2AA7 + RACP under the CGM service. toReading(): parse the record; if glucoseMgDl is non-finite (an SFLOAT sentinel) throw "SG is a non-finite SFLOAT sentinel (no value)"; round to Int; if mgDl < safetyLimits.minGlucoseMgDl (20) or > maxGlucoseMgDl (500) throw a MedtronicReadException — REJECT, never clamp, because a wrong SG is more dangerous than a missing one. This explicit check exists so CgmReading's own init (which re-asserts 20..500) never leaks an IllegalArgumentException to callers. Timestamp is now() (report-last returns the most recent measurement, so read time approximates capture time; per-record absolute time via CGM Session Start Time is a later refinement).
edge_cases: Open TODO(48.C2/F): the sensor-status annunciation (CgmMeasurement.status) is NOT yet gated, so a sensor in warm-up or error can still surface an SG.
The CGM Feature flag is re-read on every call (acceptable for a single-shot read; caching belongs with polling).

capabilities.name: CGM trend-arrow mapping
capabilities.behavior: trendArrowFor(ratePerMin: Double?) maps the CGM rate of change (mg/dL/min) onto the app-wide 7-state CgmTrend. null or non-finite -> UNKNOWN. |rate| < 1.0 -> FLAT. Rising: |rate| >= 3.0 -> DOUBLE_UP, >= 2.0 -> SINGLE_UP, else FORTY_FIVE_UP. Falling: >= 3.0 -> DOUBLE_DOWN, >= 2.0 -> SINGLE_DOWN, else FORTY_FIVE_DOWN. Thresholds follow the 780G manual (1-2 / 2-3 / >3 mg/dL/min = 1/2/3 arrows), folding Medtronic's three-arrow scale onto the Dexcom-style enum. A measurement whose trend-present flag is clear yields null -> UNKNOWN. Trend is only magnitude-bucketed, which is exactly why MedtronicCodec special-cases the reserved SFLOAT codes as non-finite — otherwise a "no value" sentinel would decode into a bogus arrow.
edge_cases: CGM readings extracted from HISTORY records always carry CgmTrend.UNKNOWN — the SG history record has no rate-of-change field.

capabilities.name: CGM Measurement record parser (SIG GSS 3.43)
capabilities.behavior: parse(record, useCrc). Mandatory prefix 6 bytes: size(1) + flags(1) + glucose SFLOAT(2) + timeOffset(2). Minimum length is 6, or 8 with CRC. The size field counts the WHOLE record including the CRC and is validated against record.size before the CRC is stripped. With useCrc, checkE2eCrc must pass and 2 bytes are stripped from the end. Flag bits: 0x01 trend present, 0x02 quality present, 0x20 warning present, 0x40 cal/temp present, 0x80 status present. Optional octets are consumed in wire order status(1), cal/temp(1), warning(1), trend(SFLOAT 2), quality(SFLOAT 2), each bounds-checked so a flag promising an absent field is rejected rather than read out of bounds. Trailing bytes after the declared fields are an error. Glucose and trend are mg/dL.
edge_cases: mmol/L decision (load-bearing): per the SIG CGM Service spec the Measurement glucose is mandated mg/dL with no per-record unit flag, and the CGM Feature characteristic carries no measurement-unit field, so a spec-compliant 700-series cannot emit mmol/L and the canonical-mg/dL invariant holds. The only residual is a proprietary Medtronic deviation. NO conversion is added until a real European mmol/L-display sample exists (hardware-blocked; tracked in #809 and #708). Revisit instruction: if such a sample appears, convert via the shared 18.0156 factor and PRESERVE the existing reject-outside-20..500 ordering.

capabilities.name: CGM Feature characteristic parser
capabilities.behavior: Expected length exactly 6: feature field (3 bytes LE) + type/sample-location (1) + E2E-CRC (2). The spec's chicken-and-egg workaround: the flag saying whether E2E-safety is supported lives inside the otherwise CRC-protected packet, so the CRC field is ALWAYS present and set to 0xFFFF when unsupported. This implementation reads the trailing 2-byte field first and validates the CRC only when it is not the 0xFFFF sentinel, then takes e2eCrcEnabled from the feature bit (1 << 12) in the 24-bit feature word. Explicit divergence from upstream: OpenMinimed's cgm_features.py compares data[:-2] instead of the trailing two bytes against 0xFFFF, which never matches and so always validates the CRC; this port compares the actual CRC field per the documented intent. Reading this flag per pump is the fix for upstream's 780G hard-code — 680G/770G must not be assumed to use the CRC.
edge_cases: Any length != 6 or a CRC mismatch throws MedtronicReadException and fails the CGM read.

capabilities.name: MedtronicCodec: numeric decoding primitives
capabilities.behavior: readUIntLe(data, offset, n) — LE unsigned int, n bounded to 1..3 because a signed Int cannot hold a full uint32. readULongLe(data, offset, n) — n in 1..4, for the uint32 fields (record sequence, bolus start-time offset, annunciation timestamp). u32Le(value) encodes RACP sequence operands. signExtend(value, bits) with an explicit bits==32 short-circuit (Kotlin masks shift counts to 5 bits so `1 shl 32 == 1` would corrupt the result). decodeMedFloat16 (IEEE-11073 SFLOAT): 4-bit signed exponent high nibble, 12-bit signed mantissa, value = mantissa * 10^exponent via a precomputed POW10 table (exponent bias 8). decodeMedFloat32: 8-bit signed exponent in the high byte, 24-bit signed mantissa, via Math.pow. e2eCrc = CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE (poly 0x1021, init 0xFFFF, no reflection, zero final XOR); checkE2eCrc compares the trailing 2 LE bytes. CRC_SIZE = 2.
edge_cases: SAFETY: decodeMedFloat16 returns NON-FINITE Doubles for the reserved IEEE-11073 mantissa codes — 0x07FE -> +Infinity, 0x07FF -> NaN, 0x0800 (NRes) -> NaN, 0x0801 (reserved) -> NaN, 0x0802 -> -Infinity. Upstream does NOT special-case these; this port does, so callers reject them instead of surfacing a sentinel as a real glucose or trend.

decodeMedFloat32 deliberately does NOT special-case reserved codes (upstream doesn't either, and 32-bit reserved codes differ), so a garbled insulin field decodes to a bogus finite or non-finite number — every caller MUST gate it with isFinite() plus a physiological range check.
Upstream uses float(f"{m}e{e}") to minimize FP drift; the table approach is deemed immaterial because glucose rounds to Int and trend is only magnitude-bucketed.

capabilities.name: IDD Features parsing and per-model capability tiering
capabilities.behavior: IddFeatures.parse: mandatory 8-byte prefix = e2e-crc(2) + e2e-counter(1) + insulin concentration SFLOAT(2) + flags(3 LE). Bit 0 = E2E Protection Supported -> e2eProtectionEnabled. Bit 23 = Feature Extension -> another flags byte follows, folded in at shift 24, continuing while the extension byte's 0x80 continue-bit is set (a promised-but-missing byte throws). Unlike upstream, this does NOT hard-assert that the CRC/counter bytes are 0xFFFF/0 (upstream can, because the 780G leaves E2E off). MedtronicPumpModel.fromFeatureFlags: flags == 0 -> UNKNOWN; HCL bit (1<<28) clear -> MINIMED_680G; HCL set + Smart Settings bit (1<<29) set -> MINIMED_780G; HCL set without smart settings -> MINIMED_770G. supportsSmartGuard = 770G || 780G; supportsAutoCorrectionBolus = 780G only. Rationale for capability bits over the model string: the marketing name is not on the wire — DIS model is an MMT part number (e.g. "MMT-1885") never mapped upstream, so substring-matching is unreliable.
edge_cases: TODO(48.A2): confirm the exact feature-bit-to-model boundary against a real 680G/770G/780G; the inference is explicitly "the best that can be done offline".
The tier only governs interpretation/labeling and sanity logging — individual records stay flag-driven and parse safely regardless.

capabilities.name: IDD Status / IOB / active-basal parsing and validation bounds
capabilities.behavior: All three are SAKE-encrypted; the caller decrypts first, then stripIddE2e(value, useE2e) validates and strips a trailer of counter(1)+CRC(2) when E2E is on. IddStatusRecord: body must be exactly 9 bytes — therapy state(1), operational state(1), reservoir medfloat32(4), flags(1, bit0 = reservoir attached), sensor connectivity(1), sensor message state(1). IddInsulinOnBoard: SRCP request 0x03F3 -> response opcode 0x03FC; min body 7 = opcode(2)+flags(1)+IOB f32(4); flag bit0 = remaining duration(2), bit1 = IOB partial status (2+2); trailing bytes are an error. IddActiveBasalRate: request 0x0365 -> response 0x036A; min body 8 = opcode(2)+flags(1)+template(1)+rate f32(4); flag bit0 = TBR block (type 1 + adjustment f32 4 + programmed dur 2 + remaining dur 2, read past — the mandatory rate already reflects any TBR adjustment), bit1 = TBR template number(1), bit2 = basal delivery context(1).
edge_cases: SAFETY bounds, all REJECT not clamp: reservoir must be finite and 0..MAX_RESERVOIR_UNITS = 300.0 IU; IOB must be finite and 0..MAX_IOB_UNITS = 100.0 IU; basal must be finite and >= 0 and (rate*1000).roundToInt() <= safetyLimits.maxBasalRateMilliunits (default 15_000 mU/h = 15 U/h).

Enum raw codes: TherapyControlState UNDETERMINED 0x0F / STOP 0x33 / PAUSE 0x3C / RUN 0x55. OperationalState UNDETERMINED 0x0F / OFF 0x33 / STANDBY 0x3C / PREPARING 0x55 / PRIMING 0x5A / WAITING 0x66 / READY 0x96. SensorMessageState 0x00..0x0E (NO_MESSAGE, WAIT_TO_CALIBRATE, DO_NOT_CALIBRATE, CALIBRATION_REQUIRED, CALIBRATING, SEARCHING_FOR_SENSOR_SIGNAL, NO_SENSOR_SIGNAL, CHANGE_SENSOR, WARM_UP, SG_BELOW_LOWER_LIMIT, SG_ABOVE_UPPER_LIMIT, GST_BATTERY_DEPLETED, SENSOR_CONNECTED, WAITING_WARM_UP, NO_PAIRED_SENSOR). BasalDeliveryContext UNDETERMINED 0x0F / DEVICE_BASED 0x33 / REMOTE_CONTROL 0x3C / AP_CONTROLLER 0x55. Unrecognized raw values map to UNKNOWN(-1), never throw.

BasalReading.isAutomated = (context == AP_CONTROLLER); if that appears on a non-SmartGuard tier it is logged WARN but still treated as automated (data-shape sanity, not a hard failure). activityMode is always PumpActivityMode.NONE — pump activity mode is not in the IDD basal payload.
The IDD Features read is re-issued on every IOB/basal/reservoir/status call.

capabilities.name: Battery and Device Information readers (unencrypted SIG reads)
capabilities.behavior: BatteryReader reads Battery Level 0x2A19 — a plain, NOT SAKE-encrypted, single percentage byte. An empty value throws. A percentage outside 1..100 is REJECTED, not clamped; 0 is explicitly rejected as a no/empty reading (matching upstream's `0 < batt < 101`) because a pump reporting a true 0% over an active link would already be powered off, so 0x00 is spurious. BatteryStatus.isCharging is always false: the 700-series runs on a replaceable battery and exposes no charging state. DeviceInfoReader reads the pump's own DIS characteristics by UUID (model 0x2A24, serial 0x2A25, hardware 0x2A27, firmware 0x2A26, software 0x2A28, system ID 0x2A23) as plain GATT reads; strings are UTF-8 with only trailing NULs trimmed (upstream strips a fixed terminator byte; trimming only NULs avoids truncating a value that isn't null-terminated); the 8-byte System ID is rendered as lower-case hex.
edge_cases: These two are the only reads that need no live SAKE session (gateway.blockingRead), though the transport must still be connected.

capabilities.name: HistoryReader: IDD RACP record fetch
capabilities.behavior: History deliberately uses the IDD service's RACP + IDD History Data 0x108, NOT the CGM RACP and NOT the HAT service (upstream's hats.py returns Not Supported / No Records Found for every request). Opcodes/operators (decimal shown as in code): OP_REPORT_RECORDS 51 (0x33), OP_REPORT_NUMBER_OF_RECORDS 90 (0x5A), NUMBER_OF_RECORDS_RESPONSE 102 (0x66), RESPONSE_CODE 15 (0x0F), OPERATOR_NULL 15, OPERATOR_ALL_RECORDS 51, OPERATOR_WITHIN_RANGE 90, OPERATOR_LAST_RECORD 105 (0x69), FILTER_SEQUENCE_NUMBER 15, RESPONSE_SUCCESS 240 (0xF0), RESPONSE_NO_RECORDS_FOUND 6. Requests: last record = [0x33,0x69,0x0F]; count = [0x5A,0x33,0x0F]; range = [0x33,0x5A,0x0F] + u32LE(firstSeq) + u32LE(lastSeq). Terminators: success = [0x0F,0x0F,0x33,0xF0]; no-records = [0x0F,0x0F,0x33,0x06] (treated as a SUCCESSFUL empty list — the gateway's paging walk relies on it to find the oldest retained record). readRecordCount parses response[0]==0x66 && response[1]==0x0F then a 2-byte LE count.
edge_cases: A "no records found" terminator that arrives AFTER frames were streamed is a self-contradiction and FAILS the read (trusting either side risks stale/misordered data or silently dropped records).

ANY undecodable frame in a page fails the whole page rather than silently shrinking it — the walk advances past this window and callers advance their cursor to the max sequence seen, so a dropped record would be skipped for good (this is bolus history feeding IOB). Checked BEFORE dedup, since duplicate frames legitimately shrink the list.
A flush-recovered final record is validated by MedtronicHistoryParser.isStructurallyCompleteRecordFrame before acceptance.

capabilities.name: History record framing, event types and per-event parsing
capabilities.behavior: Record header is 8 bytes: event_type u16 + sequence u32 + relative_offset u16, then the event body, optionally wrapped in the Medtronic E2E trailer. toHistoryLogRecord() preserves the E2E-STRIPPED body base64'd in HistoryLogRecord(sequenceNumber = seq.toInt(), rawBytesB64, eventTypeId, pumpTimeSeconds = relativeOffset). Event type IDs: REFERENCE_TIME 0x000F, BOLUS_PROGRAMMED_P1 0x005A, BOLUS_PROGRAMMED_P2 0x0066, BOLUS_DELIVERED_P1 0x0069, BOLUS_DELIVERED_P2 0x0096, DELIVERED_BASAL_RATE_CHANGED 0x0099, MAX_BOLUS_AMOUNT_CHANGED 0x03FC, AUTO_BASAL_DELIVERY 0xF001, CL1_TRANSITION 0xF002, THERAPY_CONTEXT 0xF004, MEAL 0xF005, BG_READING 0xF007, CALIBRATION_COMPLETE 0xF008, CALIBRATION_REJECTED 0xF009, INSULIN_DELIVERY_STOPPED 0xF00A, INSULIN_DELIVERY_RESTARTED 0xF00B, SG_MEASUREMENT 0xF00C, CGM_ANALYTICS_DATA_BACKFILL 0xF00D, NGP_REFERENCE_TIME 0xF00E, ANNUNCIATION_CLEARED 0xF00F, ANNUNCIATION_CONSOLIDATED 0xF010, MAX_AUTO_BASAL_RATE_CHANGED 0xF01A, UNDEFINED 0xFFFF.
edge_cases: Body layouts: bolus amounts (>=13B) bolus_id u16 @0, type @2, fast f32 @3, extended f32 @7, duration u16 @11. Bolus programmed P2 flags bit0 delay-time(2), bit1 template(1), bit2 activation(1), bit3 = correction reason, bit4 = meal reason. Bolus delivered P2 (>=5B) flags @0, start_time_offset u32 @1, then bit0 = activation type(1) — a DIFFERENT flag layout from programmed. Basal-rate-changed (>=9B) flags @0, old f32 @1, new f32 @5, optional context @9 when bit0 set and size>=10. Auto-basal micro-bolus (>=5B) bolusNumber u8 @0, amount f32 @1. SG measurement (>=8B) time_offset i16 @0 (sign-extended), sg u16 @2, isig u16, v_counter i16. BG reading (>=4B) time_offset i16 @0, bg SFLOAT @2 in kg/L converted to mg/dL by * 1e5. Annunciation consolidated (>=10B) event_flags @0, annunciation_id u16 @1, type u16 @3 (must have high nibble 0xF000 else throw; stored masked & 0x0FFF), status @5, timestamp u32 @6 = seconds since 2000-01-01T00:00:00Z. Annunciation cleared (>=4B) raw type u16 @0, statusRaw = CLEARED_NO_STATUS (-1), timestamp null.

BolusActivationType raw: UNDETERMINED 0x0F, MANUAL 0x33, RECOMMENDED 0x3C, MANUALLY_CHANGED_RECOMMENDED 0x55, COMMANDED 0x5A (= closed-loop/SmartGuard). HistoryBasalDeliveryContext raw: 0x0F/0x33/0x3C/ARTIFICIAL_PANCREAS_CONTROLLER 0x55.

parseRecordBody catches only MedtronicReadException and IllegalArgumentException and degrades the event to Unparsed (preserving the record); a broader catch would mask programming errors as bad data. isStructurallyCompleteRecordFrame re-runs the typed parse WITHOUT that fallback, and accepts unhandled types (they extract as Unparsed either way and feed no dosing math).

capabilities.name: History timestamp resolution (relative offsets + NGP reference time)
capabilities.behavior: Records carry only a relative offset; absolute time is resolved by walking records in sequence order and carrying the most recent NGP_REFERENCE_TIME forward. Reference-time body (>=8B): recording_reason(1) then year u16 @1, month @3, day @4, hour @5, minute @6, second @7. The pump stores this as NAIVE LOCAL wall-clock with no TZ/DST field (it is set to the user's local time), so it is anchored via LocalDateTime.atZone(ZoneId.systemDefault()).toInstant(). Documented reason: interpreting it as UTC shifts every history timestamp by the local offset (into the future east of UTC, e.g. +2h in CEST). A java.time.DateTimeException yields a null reference (logged) and offsets after it cannot be anchored. Each event's absolute time = reference.plusSeconds(relativeOffsetSeconds). Records seen BEFORE any reference time, or whose body fails to parse, are DROPPED (counted, logged at VERBOSE because all three extractors call timedRecords on the same batch) rather than mis-timestamped.
edge_cases: Explicitly UNRESOLVED: DST gap/overlap hours, and a phone timezone that differs from the pump's, are inherently ambiguous.
Annunciation timestamps use a different, absolute epoch (2000-01-01T00:00:00Z + seconds), not the reference-time mechanism.

capabilities.name: Domain extraction from history (CGM / bolus / basal) and the SmartGuard exclusion
capabilities.behavior: extractCgmFromHistoryLogs: SG_MEASUREMENT events only; SG_SENTINELS = {0x0301, 0x0303, 0x030D} are dropped; readings outside limits.minGlucoseMgDl..maxGlucoseMgDl are DROPPED, never clamped; trend is always UNKNOWN; sorted by timestamp. extractBolusesFromHistoryLogs: BOLUS_DELIVERED_P1 only (programmed is skipped); total = fastIu + extendedIu, dropped if non-finite or < 0, dropped if (total*1000).roundToInt() > limits.maxBolusDoseMilliunits (default 25_000 mU), and dropped if total > BolusEvent.MAX_BOLUS_UNITS (25f) so the domain init's require never throws. isAutomated comes from the immediately-following BOLUS_DELIVERED_P2 activation == COMMANDED (a positional heuristic; a dropped/interleaved record degrades to manual). correction/meal reason is joined by bolus id from the programmed-P1 -> programmed-P2 pair. extractBasalFromHistoryLogs: DELIVERED_BASAL_RATE_CHANGED newRate; non-finite/<0 dropped; > limits.maxBasalRateMilliunits dropped; isAutomated = context == ARTIFICIAL_PANCREAS_CONTROLLER.
edge_cases: DELIBERATE OMISSION (load-bearing): AUTO_BASAL_DELIVERY (0xF001) SmartGuard auto-correction micro-boluses on 770G/780G are NOT mapped to bolus events. Stated reason: how they should be attributed (bolus vs basal, double-count risk) is unresolved without live validation, so they are counted and logged at DEBUG rather than guessed. Revisit trigger: TODO(48.A2) live validation. The user doc mirrors this: "SmartGuard auto-basal micro-boluses are not yet fully attributed".

Medtronic reports only the delivered TOTAL with no numeric correction/meal split, so correctionUnits = total only when correction && !meal, mealUnits = total only when meal && !correction, and BOTH are 0 when neither or both reasons are set.

capabilities.name: MedtronicDevicePlugin: capability surface and pairing UX contract
capabilities.behavior: Metadata: id "com.glycemicgpt.medtronic", name "Medtronic MiniMed Pump", version "1.0.0", apiVersion PLUGIN_API_VERSION, protocolName "Medtronic", description "Medtronic MiniMed 700-series pumps (680G / 770G / 780G) over Bluetooth (read-only, BETA)". Capabilities: GLUCOSE_SOURCE, INSULIN_SOURCE, PUMP_STATUS only. pairingProfile = PairingProfile(ADVERTISE_AND_WAIT, advertisedName = "Mobile 000001"). observeConnectionState() proxies the manager's StateFlow; observePairingFault() maps MedtronicConnectionFault -> PairingFault 1:1 (needed because several faults produce no state transition, so the UI would otherwise have nothing to show). connect(address, config) ignores address and calls startSession(forceFirstPair = config["forceFirstPair"].toBoolean()). scan() proxies the manager's advertise-and-wait flow. settingsDescriptor() contributes exactly one item: a "Connection" section InfoText keyed "single_peer_note" stating a MiniMed pump pairs with only one phone at a time and must be removed from the official Medtronic app first. observeDashboardCards() emits an empty list.
edge_cases: initialize(context) is a no-op (BLE components are injected ready-to-use).
shutdown() calls connectionManager.close() (terminal: releases the worker thread and cancels the scope); onDeactivated() calls disconnect() so the plugin can be reactivated without re-pairing.

capabilities.name: Capability delegates: glucose, insulin (bolus cursor), pump status
capabilities.behavior: MedtronicGlucoseSource.observeReadings() is a naive `while(true) { getCgmReading().onSuccess { emit } ; delay(POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 60_000) }` loop; getCurrentReading() is a direct gateway call. MedtronicInsulinSource: getIoB()/getBasalRate() proxy the gateway. getBolusHistory(since, limits) runs entirely under a bolusSyncMutex so the read-fetch-advance of the in-memory `bolusCursor: Int?` is atomic. Bootstrap: on the first call of the process, gateway.getHistoryCursor() (one read-last-record exchange, no paging) seeds the cursor past all existing history and returns an EMPTY list; an empty pump log seeds 0. Subsequent calls fetch getHistoryLogs(sinceSequence = cursor), set cursor = max sequence seen (or keep the old cursor if the page is empty), extract delivered boluses via MedtronicHistoryParser applying `limits`, and filter to timestamps not before `since`. MedtronicPumpStatus proxies battery/reservoir/settings/hardware/history and exposes the three pure extract* helpers plus unpair()/autoReconnectIfPaired().
edge_cases: bolusCursor is explicitly BEST-EFFORT, not the durable record: it advances on a successful fetch before the orchestrator persists, so a transient save failure could skip a bolus on this path. Tolerated because the orchestrator's slow-loop raw-history sync is the durable, self-healing bolus path (persists each raw HistoryLogRecord to Room keyed by sequence before advancing its own cursor, restores it on restart, re-extracts the same boluses).
Each process restart re-seeds from the pump's latest sequence rather than rescanning; boluses delivered while the app was down reach the platform via the slow loop's backfill.
observeReadings' 60s cadence is superseded in practice by the app's PumpPollingOrchestrator (fast 15s, medium 300s, slow 300s), which is a separate subsystem.

capabilities.name: Device-info mapping onto the shared (Tandem-shaped) domain models
capabilities.behavior: toPumpSettings() is the faithful lossless mapping: firmwareVersion = firmwareRevision, serialNumber, modelNumber carried across verbatim as strings. toPumpHardwareInfo() is an explicitly lossy best-effort adaptation because PumpHardwareInfo's identity fields are Long while Medtronic's are alphanumeric: serialNumber/modelNumber/armSwVer are numericId(...) = the numeric value of the LONGEST run of digits in the string ("MMT-1880" -> 1880, "NG1234567H" -> 1234567), 0 when there are no digits, and truncated to the trailing 18 digits (MAX_LONG_DIGITS) to avoid Long overflow. pumpRev = firmwareRevision, pcbaRev = hardwareRevision. partNumber, mspSwVer, configABits, configBBits, pcbaSn are left 0 and pumpFeatures is left EMPTY — deliberately, because pumpFeatures is a feature-flag map uploaded verbatim to the backend as `pump_features` and must not be repurposed to smuggle identity strings.
edge_cases: TODO(48.D): prefer surfacing MedtronicDeviceInfo/toPumpSettings directly to the dashboard once the UI consumes pump identity, rather than round-tripping through the lossy Long-keyed view.
Medtronic exposes no dedicated settings characteristic, so both settings and hardware info derive from DIS.

capabilities.name: Hilt DI wiring and lifecycle ownership
capabilities.behavior: MedtronicPumpModule (SingletonComponent) @Binds @IntoSet MedtronicPluginFactory into the platform's Set<PluginFactory> so PluginRegistry discovers it. Singleton providers: MedtronicPeripheral = AndroidMedtronicPeripheral(appContext); SerialWorker = HandlerThreadSerialWorker("medtronic-sake"); MedtronicBleConnectionManager(peripheral, credentialStore, worker, CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + Dispatchers.IO)); AndroidMedtronicGattLink(context, deviceProvider = { connectionManager.connectedPumpDevice }, worker = the SAME SerialWorker so inbound notifications stay serialized with SAKE work); MedtronicReadGateway(sessionProvider = { connectionManager.sakeSession }, linkProvider = { if (connectionManager.connectionState.value == ConnectionState.CONNECTED) gattLink else null }). The gated linkProvider is the mechanism by which every read reports a clean "not connected" failure rather than reading a dead link or fabricating data.
edge_cases: The module's manifest merges BLUETOOTH_ADVERTISE (tools:targetApi="s") and BLUETOOTH_CONNECT into the app manifest; the host app requests them at runtime. Below API 31 ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION is also required (declared by the host).

capabilities.name: User-facing pairing procedure (what the user must do ON THE PUMP)
capabilities.behavior: Documented flow: (1) In the app, open pump settings and choose Medtronic. (2) Open Pump Pairing; a "Before you start" note explains removing the pump from the manufacturer's app. (3) Tap Start Pairing — the phone becomes discoverable as "Mobile 000001" and shows "Waiting for your pump." (4) ON THE PUMP, open the Bluetooth pairing menu (Add / Pair new device) and select "Mobile 000001." (5) Confirm the pairing on the pump if prompted. The app moves waiting -> connecting -> connected. Prerequisite: the pump MUST first be removed from MiniMed Mobile or any other phone — a MiniMed pump pairs with only one phone at a time. Once paired, the pump is remembered and GlycemicGPT reconnects on its own when it is back in range. Read-only is stated explicitly: no boluses, no basal changes, no setting changes, no Medtronic account, no cloud, no browser step.
edge_cases: Documented failure messages with Try Again: "No pump has connected yet." (BOUND_ELSEWHERE), "This phone can't act as a Bluetooth accessory." (PERIPHERAL_UNSUPPORTED), "Couldn't start Bluetooth advertising." (ADVERTISE_FAILED), "The secure handshake timed out" / "the pump rejected the secure handshake." (HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT / AUTH_FAILED).

Doc states what it reads: sensor glucose, IoB, active basal rate, bolus history, reservoir, pump battery. Explicit caveats: SmartGuard auto-basal micro-boluses are not yet fully attributed; IoB is read straight off the pump and has been confirmed against a live 780G's on-screen Active Insulin (subject to display rounding).

capabilities.name: tools/medtronic-ble-spike: offline de-risk harness
capabilities.behavior: A standalone JVM Gradle project (not part of the app build, own settings.gradle.kts, application plugin, Java 11 target, JDK 17+ required by the Gradle 9.1 wrapper) that proves two gating unknowns with NO physical pump. (1) The SAKE handshake on the JVM: org.openminimed:javasake:0.2.0 completes the 6-stage handshake with the phone in MOBILE_APPLICATION (SAKE-server) role and the pump as INSULIN_PUMP client, validated byte-for-byte against OpenMinimed's captured 780G pairing trace; SeqCrypt encrypt/decrypt round-trips and rejects tampering. `./gradlew test` is the acceptance gate; `./gradlew run` narrates stage-by-stage and prints "SUMMARY: 16 passed, 0 failed -> ALL CHECKS PASSED". Files: SakeTestVectors.java (capture + matched pair), QueuedRngSource.java (deterministic RNG replaying a captured trace), SakeSpikeHarness.java, MedtronicSakeSpikeTest.java. (2) android-peripheral-probe/PeripheralModeProbe.kt: reference-only Android code recording advertiser presence, isMultipleAdvertisementSupported, openGattServer+addService(0xFE82) success and startAdvertising outcome into a PeripheralCapability.
edge_cases: Known harness limitation: `./gradlew run` lives outside the org.openminimed.sake package so it cannot set the package-private msg4 pad byte; it validates msg0/msg2 bytes + full completion + live cipher round-trip and defers exact msg4 byte-parity to upstream's in-package JUnit suite. The emitted msg4's first 16 bytes (the encrypted permit) DO match the capture; only the pad-dependent 4-byte trailer differs, which does not affect completion.

Support matrix: the Android emulator is an authoritative KNOWN-NEGATIVE — its Bluetooth stack has no radio, getBluetoothLeAdvertiser() returns null, so no central can ever connect. Physical device rows are TBD pending the hardware-gated follow-up.

Implementation notes carried into production: advertise -> connect -> stop advertising -> restart on disconnect; serialize SAKE off the binder thread on a HandlerThread; 20-byte zero wake-up on CCCD subscribe; graceful degradation with a clear message when isPeripheralCapable is false.

safety_critical: GLUCOSE VALIDATION — REJECT, NEVER CLAMP. CgmReader rejects any SG outside SafetyLimits 20..500 mg/dL with a MedtronicReadException before constructing CgmReading (whose init re-asserts 20..500). History-extracted CGM readings outside the same bounds are DROPPED. A wrong SG is explicitly deemed more dangerous than a missing one. The Swift port must preserve reject-not-clamp and the ordering (sentinel check -> round -> range check).

SFLOAT SENTINEL HANDLING. decodeMedFloat16 returns NaN/±Infinity for the reserved IEEE-11073 mantissa codes 0x07FE, 0x07FF, 0x0800, 0x0801, 0x0802 — a divergence from upstream added specifically so a 'no value' sentinel cannot surface as a real glucose or as a bogus trend arrow (trend is only magnitude-bucketed). CgmReader explicitly rejects non-finite glucose. Losing this in the port silently turns sentinels into readings.

MEDFLOAT32 HAS NO SENTINEL HANDLING. decodeMedFloat32 (used for reservoir, IOB, basal rate, bolus units) deliberately does NOT special-case reserved codes. Every caller MUST gate with isFinite() plus a physiological range check: reservoir 0..300 IU, IOB 0..100 IU, basal >= 0 and <= SafetyLimits.maxBasalRateMilliunits (15_000 mU/h), bolus total <= maxBolusDoseMilliunits (25_000 mU) and <= BolusEvent.MAX_BOLUS_UNITS (25 U). Dropping any of these gates lets a garbled read surface as a real insulin/reservoir number.

UNIT CONVERSION. Glucose is canonical mg/dL end to end; NO mmol/L conversion exists in this driver and one must not be added without a real European mmol/L-display sample (documented decision, tracked in #809/#708). If ever added, use the shared 18.0156 factor and preserve the reject-outside-20..500 ordering. History BG readings ARE converted: SFLOAT kg/L * 1e5 = mg/dL. Basal/bolus math converts IU to milliunits by *1000 then roundToInt before comparing to limits.

HISTORY CURSOR SKIP HAZARD (the single most dangerous class of bug here). Multiple layers exist solely to stop a history cursor advancing past data the pump actually sent, which would permanently lose bolus records feeding IOB: (a) any undecodable frame in a page fails the whole page; (b) a failed page fails the whole getHistoryLogs call rather than returning partial newer pages; (c) the paging walk is driven by the requested window, never by page content; (d) a flush-recovered unterminated final record must pass isStructurallyCompleteRecordFrame or the exchange fails loudly; (e) a 'no records found' terminator arriving after streamed frames fails the read. All five must be reproduced.

BLE PROTOCOL CORRECTNESS — UUID BASES. The Medtronic vendor base uses variant field 0000 (0000XXXX-0000-1000-0000-009132591325), not the SIG 8000. The SAKE characteristic must be vendor-base 0xFE82 while the service is SIG-base 0xFE82, and the phone's DIS container must be vendor 0x0900 not SIG 0x180A. Getting either wrong causes the pump to find the service but not the characteristic, so the handshake never begins and no data is ever read (issue #844).

RACP SERVICE SCOPING. The SIG 0x2A52 RACP is exposed under BOTH the CGM and IDD services. Resolving it to the wrong service silently reads the wrong log — i.e. glucose data interpreted as insulin history or vice versa. The implementation prefers the last-resolved RACP-bearing service, falls back to an actively-subscribed service, and THROWS rather than guessing. It also refuses to let a Battery/Device-Info read move the scoping context.

STALENESS / TIMESTAMPS. CGM and IDD status readings are stamped with the phone's now() at read time, NOT a pump-provided capture time (report-last-record returns the most recent measurement; per-record absolute time via CGM Session Start Time is a deferred refinement). History records carry only relative offsets anchored to a naive-local NGP reference time interpreted in ZoneId.systemDefault(); DST gap/overlap and a phone/pump timezone mismatch are explicitly unresolved. Records before any reference time are dropped rather than mis-timestamped.

SENSOR STATUS NOT YET GATED. Open TODO(48.C2/F) in CgmReader: the CGM Measurement status/annunciation byte is parsed but NOT used, so a sensor in warm-up or an error state can still surface a misleading SG. SensorMessageState (WARM_UP, NO_SENSOR_SIGNAL, CHANGE_SENSOR, SG_BELOW/ABOVE_LIMIT, etc.) is decoded in the IDD status path but not wired into glucose gating.

READ-ONLY GUARANTEE. Three independent layers: the transport's WRITABLE_CONTROL_POINTS allow-list (RACP, CGM SOCP, IDD SRCP only), only GET/report-class opcodes constructed anywhere, and a plugin that declares no control capability. Any weakening of the allow-list makes a therapeutic write physically possible. Note the documented revisit trigger: introducing ANY write/therapeutic surface requires raising the SAST/threat model.

SMARTGUARD MICRO-BOLUS ATTRIBUTION GAP. AUTO_BASAL_DELIVERY (0xF001) events are deliberately excluded from bolus extraction because bolus-vs-basal attribution and double-count risk are unvalidated. On 770G/780G this means displayed bolus history under-reports delivered insulin. The user doc states this. Do not 'fix' it in the port by guessing an attribution.

BOLUS ACTIVATION CORRELATION IS A POSITIONAL HEURISTIC. isAutomated is taken from the record immediately following BOLUS_DELIVERED_P1 in sequence order; a dropped or interleaved record makes the join miss and the bolus silently degrade to manual/non-correction rather than failing. Correction/meal reason is joined by bolus id across programmed-P1/P2. Whole mapping is flagged TODO(48.A2).
BATTERY 0% IS REJECTED. Valid range is 1..100; 0x00 is treated as spurious (a pump at true 0% over an active link would be powered off). isCharging is hard-coded false.

SESSION CIPHER SEQUENCE DESYNC. Each notification PDU is individually SAKE-encrypted with its own 3-byte trailer and decrypting advances a sequence counter. A late or duplicate notification decrypted after an exchange finishes would consume the next operation's sequence slot and desync the session (guarded by per-exchange `finished` flags, the subscription watchdog, and the gateway's single-flight mutex). All three guards are load-bearing.

AUTH_FAILED IS LATCHED. A terminal handshake failure must not be reset by the inevitable pump disconnect and must not start a reconnect loop against a pump that just rejected us; the user has to re-pair. Advertising is stopped on both the auth-failure and handshake-timeout paths.
