port.subsystem: Medtronic MiniMed 680G/770G/780G read-only BLE driver — phone-as-peripheral (CBPeripheralManager) + SAKE session + CGM/IDD/history read layer + driver capability surface, plus the offline SAKE de-risk harness and the user pairing doc.

ports_cleanly.capability: UUID base scheme: SIG base vs Medtronic vendor base (issue #844 fix)
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: CBUUID accepts arbitrary 128-bit UUID strings for both local (peripheral-role) and remote (central-role) services and characteristics, with no variant-field validation. Build the two bases as string constants exactly as Kotlin does: SIG 0000XXXX-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb and vendor 0000XXXX-0000-1000-0000-009132591325 (variant 0000, not 8000). Keep the same split: SAKE service on the SIG base 0xFE82, SAKE characteristic on the vendor base 0xFE82, phone-exposed DIS container on vendor 0x0900. Note CBUUID normalizes 16-bit-shaped SIG UUIDs to their short form in description output only; identity comparison is unaffected. Port MedtronicProtocol as a single Swift enum of static CBUUIDs with a golden unit test asserting all 128-bit expansions byte-for-byte.

ports_cleanly.capability: Full GATT UUID inventory (SAKE, DIS, CGM, Battery, IDD, HAT, CM, RACP, CCCD)
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Direct constant translation. One iOS-specific deletion: CCCD 0x2902 must NOT appear in the local GATT table (Core Bluetooth owns it — see the subscribe/unsubscribe entry). Keep HAT 0x300 and CM 0x600 declared-but-unused with the same comments so the deliberate non-use survives the port. RACP 0x2A52 stays shared across CGM and IDD.

ports_cleanly.capability: Phone-side GATT server registration order and placeholder DIS values
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: CBMutableService/CBMutableCharacteristic; call add(_:) one service at a time and chain on peripheralManager(_:didAdd:error:), same ConcurrentLinkedQueue discipline (a Swift array + index on the driver's serial queue). Defer startAdvertising until the last didAdd succeeds; a didAdd error maps to the synthetic GATT_SERVER_UNAVAILABLE (-2) fault exactly as today — still the one step with no timeout, so the fault path is load-bearing. DIS placeholders port verbatim, declared as read-only characteristics with static values (Core Bluetooth requires cached-value characteristics be read-only, which the DIS set already is). The SAKE characteristic must have value nil (dynamic) because it is notify+write.

ports_cleanly.capability: SAKE CCCD subscribe/unsubscribe detection
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Strictly better on iOS. Core Bluetooth manages the CCCD itself and delivers peripheralManager(_:central:didSubscribeTo:) and didUnsubscribeFrom:, so the whole byte-sniffing branch (value[0] & 0x01, the 0x00/0x00 disable pattern, the 'unexpected, ignoring' case) collapses into two delegate methods. The ungated onDescriptorReadRequest workaround for issue #844 becomes unnecessary and must be deleted, not translated. Gate both callbacks on characteristic.uuid == vendor 0xFE82. didSubscribeTo is the cue to emit the 20-byte zero wake-up frame.

ports_cleanly.capability: Characteristic write and read request handling on the local server
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: peripheralManager(_:didReceiveWrite requests:) forwards request.value verbatim to the SAKE driver, then respond(to: requests[0], withResult: .success) once for the batch. peripheralManager(_:didReceiveRead request:) honors request.offset with the same bounds rule, responding .invalidOffset when offset < 0 or > value.count, else setting request.value to the offset slice and responding .success. Core Bluetooth handles ATT blob-read continuation when you respond correctly.

ports_cleanly.capability: Connection state machine (7 states + transitions)
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Pure logic; port as-is onto a single serial DispatchQueue. Substitutions: 'pump connected to the GATT server' becomes the first didSubscribeTo (Core Bluetooth surfaces no connect event for a central attaching to your peripheral — subscription is the earliest observable), and 'pump disconnected' becomes didUnsubscribeFrom plus a CBCentralManager disconnect on the client link. Keep AUTH_FAILED sticky, keep stopAdvertising on connect (single-peer), keep autoReconnect=false on both failure paths, keep the synchronous close()-on-caller-thread teardown.

ports_cleanly.capability: Connection faults and their timers
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: MedtronicConnectionFault ports as a Swift enum published alongside connection state (two separate streams, because several faults produce no state change). Timers port to Task.sleep races or DispatchSourceTimer on the serial queue: 30_000 ms handshake timeout armed on AUTHENTICATING, 60_000 ms pairing wait armed only for FIRST_PAIR advertising, RECONNECT waiting indefinitely. Both re-check state on the driver queue before firing. PERIPHERAL_UNSUPPORTED remaps to CBManagerState .unsupported/.unauthorized/.poweredOff (see the capability-gate entry) but keeps its identity in the enum and in the UI mapping.

ports_cleanly.capability: Peripheral capability gate (isSupported)
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Android's isMultipleAdvertisementSupported / bluetoothLeAdvertiser != null check has no analogue: every iPhone Apple currently supports can act as a BLE peripheral. Replace with CBManagerState from peripheralManagerDidUpdateState: .unsupported (which is what the iOS Simulator always reports) and .unauthorized map to PERIPHERAL_UNSUPPORTED; .poweredOff maps to a distinct 'Bluetooth is off' fault. The user-facing string 'This phone can't act as a Bluetooth accessory.' should be re-worded for iOS since the real causes are Simulator, Bluetooth off, or permission denied.

ports_cleanly.capability: Discovery is advertise-and-wait, not a scan
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: scan() becomes an AsyncThrowingStream (or AsyncStream of Result) with the same semantics: check CBManagerState, install a discovery hook, set autoReconnect=false, start FIRST_PAIR advertising in state SCANNING, tear down on termination only if still SCANNING. DiscoveredDevice.name stays the phone's own advertised name. DiscoveredDevice.address changes meaning: iOS never exposes a peer BLE MAC, so it carries CBCentral.identifier (an opaque per-app UUID). Keep the rule that a discovered pump cannot be 'connected to later'.

ports_cleanly.capability: SAKE handshake wire choreography (SakeHandshakeDriver)
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Pure state machine over the transport seam; ports line-for-line onto the serial queue. Keep all four flags (session, pumpSubscribed, complete, failed), the mid-handshake session rebuild when stage != 0, the latched failure so onAuthFailed fires exactly once, the ignore-after-complete rule, and the invariant that the wake-up frame is emitted outside the state machine and never fed into onPumpWrite. Swift errors replace exceptions; catch a typed SakeError, not a blanket catch.

ports_cleanly.capability: SerialWorker: single-thread serialization discipline
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: One serial DispatchQueue ('medtronic-sake', .userInitiated) passed as the delegate queue to BOTH CBPeripheralManager and CBCentralManager, so every Core Bluetooth callback already arrives serialized on it — a structural improvement over Android's binder-thread hop. Share the same queue instance across the connection manager, handshake driver and client transport so the reader's lock-free per-exchange state stays valid. Do not use a Swift actor here: actors give no FIFO ordering guarantee, and the reader relies on submission-order delivery. Blocking this queue is forbidden (see the transport redesign entry).

ports_cleanly.capability: MTU policy and 20-byte outbound PDU framing (PduFramer)
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: iOS negotiates ATT MTU automatically and exposes no requestMtu on either role, which matches the driver's 'never request MTU' policy exactly. Keep MAX_PDU_SIZE = 20 for all outbound notifications and reads (safe under any negotiated MTU); CBCentral.maximumUpdateValueLength is observational only, the analogue of onMtuChanged. Port fragment/reassemble verbatim including the empty-payload-yields-one-empty-chunk rule. One additive iOS requirement: updateValue(_:for:onSubscribedCentrals:) returns false when the transmit queue is full — queue the pending frame and resume from peripheralManagerIsReady(toUpdateSubscribers:). Android had no equivalent backpressure callback.

ports_cleanly.capability: Read-only enforcement in the transport (defense in depth)
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Port WRITABLE_CONTROL_POINTS = { RACP 0x2A52, CGM SOCP 0x2AAC, IDD SRCP vendor 0x105 } as a Swift Set<CBUUID> checked in the single write entry point, refusing anything else with a WARN and a silent return. Strengthen it for free in Swift: make the write API take a WritableControlPoint enum with three cases rather than a bare CBUUID, so a non-control-point write is a compile error, and keep the runtime allow-list as the second layer. Keep the plugin-level rule that no control capability is declared and that only GET/report-class opcodes are constructed anywhere.

ports_cleanly.capability: Shared RACP characteristic service-scoping
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Structurally easier and must still keep the throw-rather-than-guess rule. Core Bluetooth discovery is service-scoped by construction (discoverCharacteristics(_:for:)) and every CBCharacteristic carries a weak .service back-reference, so build the same index of bare UUID -> [(CBService, CBCharacteristic)] plus racpServiceUuids from the discovered tree. Preserve all three resolution rules: single candidate wins and updates lastResolvedServiceUuid only if its service exposes RACP; multiple candidates prefer lastResolvedServiceUuid, then a live subscription; otherwise throw. Preserve the rule that a Battery or DIS read cannot move the scoping context.

ports_cleanly.capability: NotificationReassembler and the exact-multiple ambiguity
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Pure logic. Port the rule set exactly: full 20-byte fragments accumulate, a short fragment terminates, an empty PDU is ignored, MAX_FRAME_SIZE = 512 resets and throws. Keep hasPartialFrame/fragmentCount/flush/reset. Keep the documented exact-multiple ambiguity and the rule that flushed bytes are indistinguishable from truncation so callers must validate. Use Data with explicit count-based indexing, never index arithmetic on a slice (Data slices carry a non-zero startIndex and this is the single most common Kotlin-to-Swift parser porting bug).

ports_cleanly.capability: MedtronicSessionReader: the six control-point exchange patterns
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Pure logic over the transport protocol. Port reportLastRecord ([0x01,0x06], terminator [0x06,0x00,0x01,0x01]), socpGet (with LE E2E-CRC), srcpGet (no E2E-CRC), decryptedRead, reportRecords (MAX_RECORDS_PER_REPORT 50_000, caller-supplied isSuccess and validateRecoveredFrame with a rejecting default), and controlPointQuery. Keep the idempotent `finished` flag per exchange, unsubscribing both characteristics on finish, the deliberate absence of any timer inside the framework, and the rule that a decrypt/MAC/length failure becomes a Result failure rather than escaping the delivery queue. Keep all three CGM/IDD flush-recovery outcomes exactly as specified.

ports_cleanly.capability: CgmReader: sensor glucose read path and safety gating
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Pure logic. Keep the ordering: read CGM Feature 0x2AA8 per pump (never hard-code 780G), reportLastRecord over 0x2AA7 + RACP scoped to the CGM service, parse, reject non-finite SFLOAT sentinel, round to Int, then reject outside SafetyLimits 20...500 — reject, never clamp. In Swift the sentinel check must come strictly before the rounding conversion because Int(Double.nan) traps at runtime rather than throwing; guard on .isFinite first and use Int(exactly:) on the rounded value. Timestamp stays Date() at read time. Carry the open TODO that sensor-status annunciation is still not gating SG.

ports_cleanly.capability: CGM trend-arrow mapping
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Pure logic, direct port: nil or non-finite -> unknown; |rate| < 1.0 -> flat; >= 3.0 -> double; >= 2.0 -> single; else fortyFive, signed by direction. Keep the note that history-extracted CGM readings always carry .unknown because the SG history record has no rate field. Port the threshold table as named constants with a unit test per bucket boundary.

ports_cleanly.capability: CGM Measurement record parser (SIG GSS 3.43) and CGM Feature parser
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Pure logic. Measurement: 6-byte mandatory prefix, size field validated against the whole record before CRC stripping, flag bits 0x01/0x02/0x20/0x40/0x80 consumed in wire order status/calTemp/warning/trend/quality, each bounds-checked, trailing bytes an error. Feature: exactly 6 bytes, read the trailing 2-byte CRC field first and validate only when it is not the 0xFFFF sentinel, then take e2eCrcEnabled from feature bit (1 << 12). Preserve the documented divergence from OpenMinimed's cgm_features.py. Preserve the mg/dL-only decision and add no mmol/L conversion. Every bounds check must be an explicit guard returning a thrown error, because Swift array/Data out-of-range subscripting traps uncatchably.

ports_cleanly.capability: MedtronicCodec numeric decoding primitives
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Pure logic with three Swift-specific hardenings. (1) decodeMedFloat16 keeps the reserved-mantissa sentinel mapping (0x07FE -> +inf, 0x07FF/0x0800/0x0801 -> nan, 0x0802 -> -inf) — this divergence from upstream is safety-critical and must survive. (2) signExtend's bits==32 short-circuit is unnecessary in Swift (Swift's shift operators are 'smart' and over-shift to 0 rather than masking the count) but keep an explicit bits==32 branch plus its test so the behavior is pinned. (3) All accumulation arithmetic must use explicitly widened types or the &+/&* operators: Swift traps on integer overflow by default, so a garbled pump byte that Kotlin tolerated would crash the app. e2eCrc is CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE, straight port.

ports_cleanly.capability: IDD Features parsing and per-model capability tiering
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Pure logic. 8-byte mandatory prefix, bit 0 = E2E supported, bit 23 = feature extension folded in at shift 24 while the 0x80 continue bit is set, promised-but-missing byte throws. Keep the deliberate absence of upstream's hard 0xFFFF/0x00 assertion. MedtronicPumpModel.fromFeatureFlags ports verbatim (flags==0 -> unknown; HCL bit 1<<28 clear -> 680G; HCL + smart-settings 1<<29 -> 780G; HCL alone -> 770G), including the rationale that DIS model is an MMT part number and must not be substring-matched. Keep the TODO that the feature-bit-to-model boundary is unconfirmed against real hardware.

ports_cleanly.capability: IDD Status / IOB / active-basal parsing and validation bounds
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Pure logic. Port stripIddE2e, the exactly-9-byte status body, the 0x03F3/0x03FC IOB exchange and the 0x0365/0x036A basal exchange with their flag-driven optional blocks, and every raw enum code table (TherapyControlState, OperationalState, SensorMessageState 0x00..0x0E, BasalDeliveryContext) mapping unrecognized values to UNKNOWN(-1) rather than throwing. All three safety bounds stay reject-not-clamp: reservoir finite and 0...300 IU, IOB finite and 0...100 IU, basal finite, >= 0, and (rate*1000).rounded() <= maxBasalRateMilliunits (15_000). Guard .isFinite before any Double-to-Int conversion. Keep isAutomated = (context == AP_CONTROLLER) with the WARN-but-accept behavior on a non-SmartGuard tier.

ports_cleanly.capability: Battery and Device Information readers (unencrypted SIG reads)
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Plain CBPeripheral.readValue(for:) with no SAKE decryption, awaited via a continuation. Battery: single byte, empty rejected, valid range 1...100 with 0 explicitly rejected as spurious, isCharging hard-coded false. DeviceInfo: read the pump's own DIS characteristics by characteristic UUID (0x2A24/0x2A25/0x2A27/0x2A26/0x2A28/0x2A23) rather than by service UUID, decode UTF-8 trimming only trailing NULs, render the 8-byte System ID as lower-case hex. These remain the only two reads that need no live SAKE session, though the client link must still be up.

ports_cleanly.capability: HistoryReader: IDD RACP record fetch
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Pure logic. Port every opcode and operator constant verbatim (0x33/0x5A/0x66/0x0F/0x69/0xF0/0x06 and the three request byte sequences), the two terminators, and readRecordCount's 0x66/0x0F + 2-byte LE parse. Keep all four failure rules: no-records-after-streamed-frames fails the read; any undecodable frame fails the whole page (checked before dedup); a flush-recovered final record must pass isStructurallyCompleteRecordFrame; no-records-found on an empty page is a successful empty list that ends the paging walk. Keep using the IDD RACP, never CGM RACP and never HAT.

ports_cleanly.capability: History record framing, event types, timestamp resolution and domain extraction
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Pure logic; the largest single body of portable code. Port the 8-byte header, the full event-type ID table, every body layout (bolus P1/P2 with their two different flag layouts, basal-rate-changed, auto-basal micro-bolus, SG measurement, BG reading kg/L * 1e5, both annunciation forms), and the reference-time walk. NGP reference time stays naive local wall-clock: anchor with DateComponents + Calendar.current in TimeZone.current, never as UTC. Records before any reference time are dropped, not mis-timestamped. Annunciation timestamps use the separate absolute 2000-01-01T00:00:00Z epoch. parseRecordBody's narrow catch (only MedtronicReadError and a typed argument error, degrading to Unparsed) becomes a typed Swift catch; isStructurallyCompleteRecordFrame re-runs without the fallback.

ports_cleanly.capability: Domain extraction safety filters and the SmartGuard exclusion
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Pure logic. Keep SG_SENTINELS {0x0301, 0x0303, 0x030D} dropped, out-of-range CGM dropped not clamped, boluses taken only from BOLUS_DELIVERED_P1 with total = fast + extended and dropped when non-finite, negative, > maxBolusDoseMilliunits (25_000 mU) or > MAX_BOLUS_UNITS (25 U), and the correction/meal split that yields 0/0 when neither or both reasons are set. Keep the positional isAutomated heuristic (immediately-following P2 activation == COMMANDED) and its documented failure mode. Critically: keep AUTO_BASAL_DELIVERY 0xF001 excluded from bolus extraction — do not invent an attribution during the port — and keep the user-facing caveat text.

ports_cleanly.capability: Capability delegates: glucose source, insulin source with bolus cursor, pump status
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Direct port. observeReadings becomes an AsyncStream driven by the same 60_000 ms loop (superseded in practice by the polling orchestrator). getBolusHistory keeps its whole read-fetch-advance under one FIFO async lock so the in-memory cursor stays atomic, keeps the first-call bootstrap that seeds past all existing history and returns empty, keeps 'empty page leaves the cursor', and keeps the explicit note that this cursor is best-effort and the orchestrator's durable raw-history sync is the self-healing path. Pump status proxies battery/reservoir/settings/hardware/history and re-exposes the three pure extract helpers.

ports_cleanly.capability: Device-info mapping onto the shared (Tandem-shaped) domain models
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Pure logic. toPumpSettings stays lossless (firmware/serial/model as strings). toPumpHardwareInfo stays the documented lossy adaptation: numericId = the longest digit run in the string, 0 when there are none, truncated to the trailing 18 digits to avoid Int64 overflow. In Swift use Int64(exactly:) or a checked initializer rather than relying on truncation semantics. Keep partNumber/mspSwVer/configABits/configBBits/pcbaSn at 0 and pumpFeatures deliberately empty so no identity string is smuggled into the backend's pump_features map.

ports_cleanly.capability: Static SAKE key-database posture
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: The posture statement carries over unchanged: these are shared protocol constants present in every 700-series pump, published upstream under GPL-3.0, not session secrets and not credentials. Embed them as a Swift constant table (or a resource in the SPM target) with the same README-level documentation so any future Swift secret scanner finding is triaged as a known published artifact. Keep the key database injectable so tests can substitute synthetic CUSTOM_* databases, and keep KEYDB_PUMP_EXTRACTED as the production default.

ports_cleanly.capability: User-facing pairing procedure documentation
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: The on-pump half of the flow is unchanged: unbind from MiniMed Mobile, open the pump's Bluetooth pairing menu, select 'Mobile 000001'. Rewrite three phone-side statements for iOS: the app must be open and in the foreground during first pairing (background iOS advertising is not discoverable by the pump); unpairing requires both an in-app 'Forget pump' and a manual Settings > Bluetooth > Forget This Device; and 'This phone can't act as a Bluetooth accessory' is replaced by Bluetooth-off / permission-denied / Simulator wording. Keep the read-only statement, the BETA label, the read-what-list, and the SmartGuard micro-bolus caveat verbatim.

needs_redesign.capability: Inverted BLE topology: phone as peripheral, and the second GATT-client connection back to the pump
needs_redesign.why: CBPeripheralManager can advertise and host a GATT server, so the peripheral half is supported. The break is the handoff: Android captures the pump's BluetoothDevice directly from the GATT-server callback and calls connectGatt on it. Core Bluetooth gives you only a CBCentral, which exposes nothing but an opaque identifier and maximumUpdateValueLength and cannot be converted into a CBPeripheral. There is no documented API to obtain a CBPeripheral for the peer that just connected to your peripheral manager, and the map's own constraint forbids a fresh scan/advertise cycle.
options: Call CBCentralManager.retrieveConnectedPeripherals(withServices: [CGM 0x181F, IDD vendor 0x100]) after SAKE completes and connect() the returned CBPeripheral — documented API, returns peers already connected at the system level, which the pump is because it connected to us.

Call retrievePeripherals(withIdentifiers: [central.identifier]) — widely observed to work because iOS derives both CBCentral.identifier and CBPeripheral.identifier from the peer's resolved identity, but Apple does not document or guarantee this equivalence.
Scan as a central for the pump and connect a second, independent link — only viable if the pump advertises at all, which is unverified and unlikely given it operates as a central.
Abandon the client link and pull everything over the SAKE characteristic — not possible; CGM/IDD/Battery/DIS data lives only on the pump's own GATT server.
needs_redesign.recommendation: Implement option 1 as primary with option 2 as automatic fallback, behind a single MedtronicPumpLinkResolver seam with a distinct fault code when both fail. This is the highest-risk unknown in the entire port and must be the first thing validated on real hardware; every parser and reader below it is worthless if the client link cannot be established.

needs_redesign.capability: Advertising contract (what the pump scans for)
needs_redesign.why: CBPeripheralManager.startAdvertising honors exactly two keys: CBAdvertisementDataLocalNameKey and CBAdvertisementDataServiceUUIDsKey. Manufacturer-specific data (company ID 0x01F9 with the 0x00||name||0x00 payload), TX power inclusion, connectable flag, advertising timeout, and the LOW_LATENCY-vs-BALANCED mode distinction between reconnect and first-pair are all unavailable. iOS also always advertises the GAP local name, inverting Android's deliberate setIncludeDeviceName(false).
options: Advertise localName = 'Mobile 000001' plus the appropriate service UUID (SIG 0xFE82 first-pair / 0xFE81 reconnect) and rely on the pump matching the GAP name against Regex('Mobile .{0,7}') — supported by the strong inference that Medtronic's own MiniMed Mobile for iOS pairs with these pumps and is subject to the identical Apple restriction.
Advertise both service UUIDs simultaneously and drop the first-pair/reconnect distinction, since iOS gives no interval control to make the distinction meaningful anyway.
Keep a manufacturerData() function in the Swift port as dead-but-documented code so the omission is explicit rather than accidental.
needs_redesign.recommendation: Advertise localName + the mode-appropriate service UUID; keep advertisingModeFor(paired, forceFirstPair) selecting only the service UUID and delete the tx-power/timeout/mode knobs with a comment naming the Apple restriction. Retain the 31-byte reasoning as a doc note only — iOS enforces the budget itself and will silently truncate a long local name.

needs_redesign.capability: GATT-client transport: serialization, blocking operations and timeouts (AndroidMedtronicGattLink)
needs_redesign.why: The Android transport takes a ReentrantLock and blocks the calling thread until the matching GATT callback fires. On iOS that pattern is fatal: Core Bluetooth delivers all callbacks on the delegate queue, so blocking that queue deadlocks the entire BLE stack, and the driver deliberately shares one serial queue across the peripheral manager, the handshake driver and the client link.
options: Rewrite every read/write/subscribe/unsubscribe as async throws using withCheckedThrowingContinuation, with a FIFO operation queue enforcing one-in-flight, and a Task.sleep race for the 10_000 ms operation timeout and 30_000 ms subscription timeout.
Keep a synchronous facade backed by a second dispatch queue and semaphores — preserves the Android shape but reintroduces the deadlock risk and burns a thread.
Model the link as a Swift actor — rejected: actors give no FIFO ordering guarantee, and the reader relies on submission-order delivery.
needs_redesign.recommendation: Go fully async/await with an explicit FIFO gate. Preserve every safety property literally: connect lazily on first use (never requestMtu, which iOS forbids anyway), publish the peripheral and service index only after discovery succeeds, reject any callback whose CBPeripheral is not the current one so a late completion cannot satisfy a later operation's slot, and keep the synthetic -1 LOCAL_TIMEOUT / -2 LOCAL_REJECTED statuses and the CBATTError-to-name mapping for WARN logs. The API 33 write-overload branch and the literal CCCD payloads disappear — setNotifyValue(_:for:) replaces both.

needs_redesign.why: The Android design exists to keep a coroutine cancellation from leaving a subscription live and desyncing the SAKE sequence counter, and it carefully defers blocking CCCD disables off kotlinx's global timeout thread. Swift's cancellation model, the absence of a global timeout thread, and setNotifyValue's async nature all change the shape, but the underlying hazard is identical and the guarantee must be preserved exactly.
options: Wrap each exchange in withTaskCancellationHandler, dropping notification handlers synchronously in the cancellation handler and enqueuing the setNotifyValue(false) calls onto the driver queue as a detached Task.

Rely on structured concurrency alone and disable notifications in a defer inside the exchange — simpler, but a cancelled task's defer runs at the next suspension point, which may be after the next exchange has already started.
Keep an explicit watchdog Task armed for 30_000 ms per subscription, mirroring SubscriptionWatchdog.
needs_redesign.recommendation: Do all three: cancellation handler drops handlers immediately (the no-dangling-notification guarantee), disables are deferred onto the driver queue, and a 30_000 ms watchdog Task backstops a subscription whose exchange never completes. Keep both identity guards verbatim — skip the disable if the peripheral was replaced by a reconnect, and skip it if the same resolved characteristic has been re-subscribed by a newer exchange.

needs_redesign.capability: MedtronicReadGateway: single-flight, timeouts and history paging
needs_redesign.why: kotlinx.coroutines.Mutex is documented FIFO-fair, and the gateway depends on that fairness so a long history backfill cannot starve a 15-second CGM keep-alive read. Swift has no fair async mutex: actors make no ordering guarantee and can reorder awaiting continuations. withTimeout and runInterruptible also have no direct Swift equivalents.
options: Implement an explicit FIFO async semaphore (a queue of continuations drained in insertion order) and use two instances for readMutex and historyMutex.
Use an actor with an internal ticket queue — same thing with more ceremony.
Use DispatchSemaphore on a dedicated queue — reintroduces blocking, rejected.
needs_redesign.recommendation: Build a small FIFOAsyncLock type and unit-test its ordering. Everything else ports as-is: resolve link and session BEFORE queueing so 'not connected' fails fast, wrap each read in a 30_000 ms timeout race producing a typed failure, keep the 200-record HISTORY_BATCH_SIZE window walk driven by the requested window and never by page content, keep empty-page-ends-the-walk, keep failed-page-fails-the-whole-call, keep the 50_000 total cap, keep releasing readMutex between pages, and keep the WARN-logs-carry-only-op-and-error-type rule (glucose, IOB, basal and reservoir values are PHI and Sentry ingests WARN).

needs_redesign.capability: Background execution, state preservation and restoration, and the absence of a foreground service
needs_redesign.why: iOS has no foreground service. An app with UIBackgroundModes bluetooth-central and bluetooth-peripheral is still suspended between BLE events and woken for roughly 10 seconds per event; Timer and DispatchQueue.asyncAfter do not fire while suspended, so the orchestrator's 15-second poll (which doubles as the keep-alive against the pump's ~30 s idle drop) cannot run on a timer in the background. State restoration relaunches the app but hands back only restored peripherals/services/advertisement data — it cannot resume arbitrary work, and the in-memory SAKE session (including its sequence counters) is unrecoverable across termination.
options: Declare both bluetooth-central and bluetooth-peripheral, set CBCentralManagerOptionRestoreIdentifierKey and CBPeripheralManagerOptionRestoreIdentifierKey, and drive polling from BLE events (didUnsubscribeFrom, didDisconnectPeripheral, notification arrival) rather than a wall clock.

Add a Live Activity as the honest replacement for Android's ongoing foreground-service notification, giving the user a persistent connection-state surface and the app a user-visible reason to be running.
Use BGAppRefreshTask as a supplementary wake — opportunistic, roughly 30 s of runtime, no guaranteed cadence, cannot substitute for a 15 s loop.
Foreground-only Medtronic operation with a local notification when the link drops — the fallback if event-driven wakes prove insufficient on hardware.
needs_redesign.recommendation: Event-driven background operation with both background modes and restoration on both managers, plus a Live Activity for connection state. Hard rule for the port: NEVER persist SAKE session cipher state — on restoration always re-run the handshake, which the existing design already supports since a pump resubscribing to the SAKE characteristic restarts it. Restoration handlers must rebuild the state machine explicitly and reassign every delegate.

needs_redesign.why: There is no MAC address on iOS. The stored 'address' becomes CBCentral.identifier / CBPeripheral.identifier, an opaque UUID that is stable per app installation and per peer bond but is NOT stable across app reinstall or after the user forgets the device in Settings. Android's savePairing(address, localName) and getPairedAddress semantics therefore change durability characteristics, and the reconnect path must survive an identifier that no longer resolves.
options: Persist the peer UUID plus the advertised local name in the Keychain with kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlock (required so a background BLE wake after reboot can read it) and treat a non-resolving identifier as 'paired but not yet seen' rather than unpaired.

Persist only the advertised local name and treat any pump that completes SAKE as the paired pump — simpler and arguably more correct given the pump binds to exactly one phone, but loses the ability to distinguish a different pump.
Store the pump's DIS serial number (read once after the first successful session) as the durable identity and use the CBCentral UUID only as a session-scoped handle.
needs_redesign.recommendation: Keychain-persist {peer UUID, advertised local name, pump DIS serial} with the serial as the durable identity and the UUID as a cache. Keep isPaired gating reconnectIfPaired, keep disconnect() preserving pairing, keep the SAKE-has-no-pairing-code note that the credential 'code' slot holds the advertised identity string, and keep the never-log-identifiers-above-DEBUG rule (it now applies to the peer UUID, not a MAC).

needs_redesign.capability: Driver registration, DI wiring and lifecycle ownership (plugin -> compile-time module)
needs_redesign.why: iOS forbids dynamic code loading, so the runtime PluginRegistry / PluginFactory / Hilt @Binds @IntoSet discovery mechanism has no iOS analogue. This is already a decided architectural change; the redesign work is preserving the capability surface and lifecycle contract on the other side of it.
options: A MedtronicDriver Swift package (SPM target) conforming to a PumpDriver protocol, listed in a static let allDrivers array in the app's composition root.
A protocol + a compile-time registry generated from a build plugin — unnecessary ceremony for a fixed, small driver set.
Fold the driver into the app target — rejected: loses the module boundary that keeps the read-only surface reviewable.
needs_redesign.recommendation: An SPM target MedtronicDriver depending on a PumpDriverAPI target (the port of :pump-driver-api: SafetyLimits, ConnectionState, CgmReading/CgmTrend, IoBReading, BasalReading, BolusEvent, BatteryStatus, ReservoirReading, PumpSettings, PumpHardwareInfo, HistoryLogRecord, PairingProfile/PairingStyle/PairingFault, PluginSettingsDescriptor). Preserve everything user-visible: id 'com.glycemicgpt.medtronic', the three capabilities GLUCOSE_SOURCE / INSULIN_SOURCE / PUMP_STATUS and nothing else, PairingProfile(ADVERTISE_AND_WAIT, 'Mobile 000001'), the fault stream published separately from the state stream, connect(address:config:) ignoring address and honoring forceFirstPair, and the single 'single_peer_note' Connection-section InfoText rendered in SwiftUI. Hilt's singleton graph becomes one composition root that owns the shared serial queue, the peripheral manager, the central manager, the connection manager, the link and the gateway, and keeps the gated linkProvider that returns nil unless state == CONNECTED.

needs_redesign.capability: JavaSake handshake and SeqCrypt — cryptographic reimplementation in Swift
needs_redesign.why: Classified as impossible to consume as a dependency (see below); what needs designing is the replacement. Apple ships no AES-CMAC: CryptoKit has HMAC and Poly1305 but no CMAC, and CommonCrypto exposes no public CMAC either. The SAKE server-role state machine (stages 0->1->3->5->6), Session, SeqCrypt with its per-direction sequence counters, KeyDatabase and DeviceType all need Swift equivalents.
options: Implement RFC 4493 AES-CMAC (~60 lines) over CommonCrypto's CCCrypt AES-ECB single-block primitive, plus AES-CTR via CCCryptorCreateWithMode, and hand-port the SAKE state machine from OpenMinimed's GPL-3.0 sources.
Depend on CryptoSwift (MIT, SPM) for CMAC — adds a third-party crypto dependency with weaker review posture and no advisory-pinning story comparable to the bcprov 1.84 pin.
Vendor swift-crypto and add CMAC there — swift-crypto tracks BoringSSL's exposed surface and does not expose CMAC.
needs_redesign.recommendation: Option 1: a self-contained MedtronicSAKE SPM target with no third-party crypto dependency, AES primitives from CommonCrypto only, and every file citing its upstream OpenMinimed source file exactly as the Kotlin port does. Preserve the phone-as-SAKE-server / pump-as-SAKE-client role assignment, HANDSHAKE_COMPLETE_STAGE = 6, MESSAGE_SIZE = 20, newWakeUpFrame() allocating fresh zeros each call, the serverCrypt-encrypts-outbound / clientCrypt-decrypts-inbound direction mapping with its CipherDirectionConfirmationTest, the throw-before-stage-6 guard, and the not-thread-safe / one-queue-only contract. The bcprov 1.84 pin and the consumer ProGuard keep rules have no iOS analogue and simply disappear.

needs_redesign.capability: Semgrep Kotlin/Java security gate and the AesEcb exclusion
needs_redesign.why: Semgrep parses Swift but ships no registry ruleset comparable to p/kotlin or p/java, so the Kotlin/Java coverage does not transfer at all. Meanwhile the Swift port will contain intentional AES-ECB (as the CMAC block primitive) that any crypto-misuse rule will flag, reproducing the original exclusion problem in a new toolchain.
options: Keep Semgrep 1.169.0 pinned and keep p/secrets (language-agnostic, still fully applicable), replace p/kotlin and p/java with a repo-authored Swift ruleset, and add gitleaks or trufflehog as a second secrets layer.
Add SwiftLint with custom rules plus swift-format for style, and Periphery for dead code — style/hygiene, explicitly not a SAST substitute.
Add MobSF as an IPA/source-level mobile SAST gate — the closest real analogue to an APK SAST gate, and the documented revisit trigger (any therapeutic write surface) should point here.

Add Swift 6 strict concurrency (-strict-concurrency=complete) with warnings-as-errors — no Android analogue, and it mechanically catches the exact data-race class this driver's serial-queue discipline exists to prevent.
needs_redesign.recommendation: Satisfy the requirement in substance: (a) Semgrep pinned, p/secrets retained, plus a repo-authored Swift rule pack whose highest-value rules are subsystem-specific — no BLE write outside the WritableControlPoint allow-list, no Double-to-Int conversion without a preceding isFinite guard, no unchecked Data subscripting in ble/read, no health value or peer identifier in a log call at warning level or above; (b) gitleaks; (c) Swift 6 strict concurrency as a hard gate; (d) MobSF wired but advisory until a write surface exists; (e) fail on HIGH/ERROR only, WARNING/INFO printed, crashed scanner fails closed — identical gate policy. Document the intentional AES-ECB in an ADR and suppress it with an annotated inline directive rather than a path exclusion, since the Swift CMAC is authored in-tree and will be patched rather than re-vendored.

needs_redesign.capability: tools/medtronic-ble-spike offline de-risk harness and the Simulator test strategy
needs_redesign.why: Core Bluetooth does not exist in the iOS Simulator (CBManagerState is always .unsupported), and the lead developer has no iPhone. The JVM spike proved two gating unknowns offline; the Swift port needs the equivalent, and iOS adds two new unknowns the JVM spike never covered (the client-link handoff and iOS-shaped advertising).
options: Port the SAKE spike to a macOS/Simulator XCTest target replaying OpenMinimed's captured 780G pairing trace through a deterministic queued RNG, asserting stage-by-stage byte parity and SeqCrypt round-trip plus tamper rejection — runs everywhere, no hardware.

Introduce a MedtronicTransport protocol seam and a MedtronicSimulatedTransport that replays recorded pump responses, so the state machine, session reader, gateway, parsers and extractors are all exercisable in the Simulator.
Build a small companion peripheral-probe app (or use a second Mac with a BLE dongle) to stand in for the pump's central role during Daniel's hardware sessions.
Rely solely on hardware validation — rejected: nobody on the team owns a MiniMed 700-series pump.
needs_redesign.recommendation: Do 1 and 2 as hard prerequisites before any hardware session — they cover the SAKE handshake, all parsers, all safety gates, the reassembler, the paging walk and the state machine, which is the large majority of the subsystem. The Android peripheral-probe README's known-negative note (emulator has no radio) becomes the iOS Simulator's equivalent and must be stated as loudly. Accept that advertising, the client-link handoff, bonding behavior and background reconnect are hardware-only.

impossible.capability: BLE advertisement manufacturer-specific data (company ID 0x01F9, payload 0x00 || ASCII(localName) || 0x00)
impossible.why: CBPeripheralManager.startAdvertising supports exactly two advertisement keys — CBAdvertisementDataLocalNameKey and CBAdvertisementDataServiceUUIDsKey. Apple provides no API to emit manufacturer-specific data, service data, or any other AD type from the peripheral role, on any iOS version, with or without an entitlement.
impossible.closest_alternative: Carry the identity in CBAdvertisementDataLocalNameKey ('Mobile 000001') alongside the mode-appropriate service UUID and rely on the pump's Regex('Mobile .{0,7}') name match. The strong supporting evidence is that Medtronic's own MiniMed Mobile for iOS pairs with these same pumps under the identical Apple restriction, which means the pump's discovery filter cannot require manufacturer data. This must nonetheless be treated as unproven until hardware-validated.

impossible.capability: Advertising mode, TX power, timeout and connectable-flag control (ADVERTISE_MODE_LOW_LATENCY vs BALANCED, ADVERTISE_TX_POWER_MEDIUM, timeout=0, setIncludeTxPowerLevel)
impossible.why: Core Bluetooth exposes no advertising interval, PHY, TX power, duty cycle, timeout or connectability parameters. iOS chooses the advertising interval itself and varies it with app state, device state and radio contention. There is no entitlement or private-adjacent API for this.
impossible.closest_alternative: Reduce advertisingModeFor(paired, forceFirstPair) to selecting only the advertised service UUID (SIG 0xFE82 first-pair vs 0xFE81 reconnect) and delete the interval/power knobs. The RECONNECT rationale (paired pumps scan infrequently and miss long advertising intervals) becomes an unmitigable risk on iOS rather than a tunable, and must be recorded as such.

impossible.capability: Discoverability by the pump while the app is backgrounded
impossible.why: When an iOS app advertises from the background, Core Bluetooth ignores CBAdvertisementDataLocalNameKey entirely and moves all service UUIDs into a proprietary 'overflow' area that only iOS devices explicitly scanning for those exact UUIDs can decode. A Medtronic pump scanning for a name matching 'Mobile .{0,7}' or for service 0xFE82 therefore cannot discover a backgrounded iPhone. This is documented Apple behavior and cannot be configured or entitled around.
impossible.closest_alternative: First-time pairing must require the app to be open and in the foreground, stated explicitly in the pairing doc and enforced in the UI (start advertising only from the visible pairing screen). For reconnection after a bond exists, the connectable advertisement is still emitted in the background and a central that reconnects by stored peer identity rather than by name will still find it — which is what Medtronic's own iOS app must rely on — but this is unverified for this pump and cannot be assumed. Provide a time-sensitive local notification prompting the user to open the app when the link has been down beyond a threshold.

impossible.capability: Programmatic bond removal on unpair (BluetoothDevice.removeBond() via reflection)
impossible.why: iOS exposes no public or private-adjacent API to remove a Bluetooth bond. Bonds are system-owned and can only be cleared by the user in Settings > Bluetooth > (i) > Forget This Device, or by erasing the device. There is no entitlement that grants this.
impossible.closest_alternative: unpair() clears the app-side Keychain pairing record, tears down advertising and the session, sets autoReconnect=false, and then presents an explicit two-step instruction to the user to forget 'Mobile 000001' (or the pump entry) in iOS Settings, ideally with a deep link to App-Prefs or at minimum a screenshot. The pairing doc and the failure-message table must both be updated, because a stale bond that the app believes is cleared is a real support-load hazard.

impossible.capability: Consuming org.openminimed:javasake:0.2.0 (and org.bouncycastle:bcprov-jdk18on:1.84) as a binary dependency
impossible.why: There is no JVM on iOS and no supported way to load or execute Java bytecode; iOS additionally forbids dynamic code loading, which is the same rule that turned the plugin architecture into compile-time modules. Neither the SAKE artifact nor BouncyCastle can be bridged, wrapped, or transpiled into a shipping iOS build.
impossible.closest_alternative: A clean-room Swift reimplementation of the SAKE state machine, Session, SeqCrypt, KeyDatabase and DeviceType, with AES-CMAC implemented per RFC 4493 over CommonCrypto's AES-ECB primitive and AES-CTR via CCCryptorCreateWithMode. GPL-3.0 permits this outright and the iOS project is GPL-3.0, so copyleft propagation remains a non-issue; each Swift file must cite its upstream OpenMinimed source file exactly as the Kotlin port does, and palmarci's attribution must carry into the iOS THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES equivalent. Acceptance is byte-parity against OpenMinimed's captured 780G pairing trace, replayed in XCTest with a deterministic RNG — the same gate the JVM spike used.

impossible.capability: Hosting the Medtronic driver on Apple Watch (watchOS as the pump's BLE peer)
impossible.why: watchOS provides no bluetooth-peripheral background mode and no supported path for sustained BLE peripheral advertising; watchOS apps are aggressively suspended outside extended runtime sessions, which are user-initiated and time-boxed. Independently of the API surface, the pump binds to exactly one phone at a time, so a watch-hosted peer would displace the iPhone rather than supplement it.
impossible.closest_alternative: The iPhone remains the sole pump peer. The Watch app receives sensor glucose, IOB, active basal, reservoir, battery and connection state over WatchConnectivity from the phone, with the backend as a secondary source when the phone is unreachable, and surfaces them in complications and the Smart Stack. Note that watchOS has no custom watch faces, so the Android watch-face path has no analogue and complications plus a Smart Stack widget are the ceiling.

ios_requirements: A user must be able to pair a MiniMed 680G/770G/780G by opening a pairing screen in the app, seeing the phone become discoverable as 'Mobile 000001', selecting that name on the pump, and watching the app move through waiting -> connecting -> connected, without entering any code, creating a Medtronic account, or using a browser.

The pairing screen must state, before the user starts, that the pump must first be removed from MiniMed Mobile or any other phone, and that the app must stay open and in the foreground for the whole first-time pairing.

The system must surface each distinct pairing failure with its own message and a Try Again action: no pump has connected yet (60 s first-pair window elapsed), Bluetooth is off or permission denied, could not start advertising, the secure handshake timed out (30 s), and the pump rejected the secure handshake.
A terminal handshake rejection must latch: the app must stop advertising, must not auto-reconnect, and must require the user to explicitly retry pairing.

Once paired, the app must reconnect to the pump on its own whenever the app is running, and must tell the user when a reconnect has not succeeded for a sustained period rather than silently showing stale data.

The app must be able to receive and serve pump-initiated Bluetooth events while backgrounded, including being relaunched into the background by the system after termination, and must re-establish a fresh secure session on every such relaunch without requiring the user to re-pair.
The system must never persist secure-session cipher state across app termination; a restored connection must always begin a new handshake.
A user must be able to unpair the pump from within the app, and the app must then instruct the user to also forget the device in iOS Settings, because the app cannot remove the Bluetooth bond itself.

The app must read, from the pump only: sensor glucose with a trend arrow, insulin on board, active basal rate, delivered bolus history, reservoir volume, pump battery percentage, and pump model/serial/firmware identity.

The app must never write any therapeutic value to the pump. This must be enforced at three independent layers: a transport allow-list permitting writes only to RACP 0x2A52, CGM SOCP 0x2AAC and IDD SRCP 0x105; construction of GET/report-class opcodes only; and a driver that declares no control capability.

The app must reject rather than clamp any out-of-range physiological value: sensor glucose outside 20–500 mg/dL, reservoir outside 0–300 IU, IOB outside 0–100 IU, basal above 15 U/h, bolus above 25 U, battery outside 1–100%.
The app must reject any value decoded from a reserved IEEE-11073 no-value sentinel and must never present it as a reading or as a trend arrow.
A malformed, truncated, or hostile pump response must produce a reported read failure, never an application crash and never a fabricated reading.

The app must never advance a history cursor past a record the pump actually sent: an undecodable frame must fail its page, a failed page must fail the whole history call, the paging walk must be driven by the requested sequence window rather than by page content, and a recovered final record must pass a structural-completeness check before acceptance.
The app must serialize all pump exchanges so that only one is in flight at a time, and must guarantee that a long history backfill cannot starve the recurring glucose read.
A cancelled or timed-out exchange must leave no live notification subscription behind, so the next exchange starts from a clean session state.
Glucose must be handled in mg/dL end to end; no mmol/L conversion may be introduced without a verified sample from a mmol/L-display pump.

History timestamps must be resolved from the pump's naive local reference time interpreted in the phone's current time zone; records with no resolvable reference time must be dropped rather than shown with a guessed time.
SmartGuard auto-basal micro-boluses must remain excluded from bolus totals, and the app must state this limitation to the user.
Pump pairing identity must persist in the Keychain with an accessibility class that permits reading after first unlock, so a background reconnect works while the device is locked.
No log line at warning level or above may contain a health value, a raw pump payload, or a peer device identifier, because warning-level logs are forwarded to error reporting.

The full driver below the Bluetooth transport — state machine, handshake, session reader, gateway, all parsers, all extractors and all safety gates — must be exercisable in the iOS Simulator against a simulated transport, and the secure-handshake implementation must be verified in CI against a captured real-pump pairing trace with no hardware present.

A maintainer must be able to fork the repository, supply their own Apple Developer credentials as repository secrets, and get a signed build delivered to their own TestFlight from GitHub Actions, with no project-published binary and no App Store submission.

The build must ship with UIBackgroundModes bluetooth-central and bluetooth-peripheral, NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription, and Core Bluetooth restore identifiers on both the central and peripheral managers.

CI must gate on: a pinned secrets scan, a repo-authored Swift static-analysis rule set covering the driver's read-only allow-list and its numeric-safety and log-redaction invariants, Swift 6 strict concurrency with warnings as errors, a committed Package.resolved treated as the lockfile, and a dependency advisory scan — failing on high-severity findings only and failing closed if a scanner crashes.

The Apple Watch must display sensor glucose, IOB, active basal, reservoir, battery and pump connection state sourced from the phone or the backend, and must never attempt to connect to the pump itself.

The connection and pairing state must be visible to the user without opening the app, via a Live Activity while a session is active and via a time-sensitive notification when the pump link has been lost long enough to matter.

risks.risk: There is no documented way to obtain a CBPeripheral for the device that just connected to your CBPeripheralManager. If neither retrieveConnectedPeripherals(withServices:) nor retrievePeripherals(withIdentifiers: [central.identifier]) yields a usable handle to the pump, the entire read layer is unreachable and the driver cannot exist on iOS even though the SAKE handshake completes.
risks.mitigation: Make this the first hardware experiment, ahead of any read-layer work. Build a minimal probe app that stands up the SAKE service, waits for a real 780G to connect and subscribe, then tries both retrieval paths and logs the outcome. Isolate the resolution behind a MedtronicPumpLinkResolver protocol so the rest of the driver is unaffected by which path wins. If both fail, the honest outcome is that Medtronic-on-iOS is blocked, and that must be known before the parser layer is built.

risks.risk: iOS cannot emit the manufacturer-specific advertisement payload the pump's discovery filter may require. If the 700-series matches on manufacturer data rather than the GAP local name, no iPhone can ever pair.
risks.mitigation: The existence of Medtronic's own MiniMed Mobile for iOS, subject to the identical Apple restriction, is strong evidence the pump matches on the GAP name and/or service UUID. Confirm on hardware in the same probe session as the link-handoff test. Do not build further pairing UX until confirmed.

risks.risk: Nobody on the team owns a MiniMed 700-series pump. The Android driver already ships as BETA and unverified on hardware, and the iOS port adds four new unverified surfaces on top: advertising shape, bonding/IO-capability behavior, the client-link handoff, and background reconnect. Every safety-critical behavior below the transport is provable offline, but nothing at the transport is.
risks.mitigation: Ship the offline SAKE parity harness and the simulated-transport test suite as hard prerequisites so the provable majority is genuinely proved. Gate the iOS Medtronic driver behind an explicit BETA/unverified flag with the same README language the Android repo uses. Prioritize recruiting a 780G tester; this is a product decision, not an engineering one.

risks.risk: iOS cannot declare a NoInputNoOutput IO capability. The pump requests MITM with legacy pairing; an iPhone presenting DisplayYesNo or KeyboardDisplay may negotiate a passkey or numeric-comparison association model instead of Just Works, producing a system pairing prompt the Android path never showed — or a pairing failure.
risks.mitigation: Do not mark any local characteristic as requiring encryption (the SAKE characteristic uses plain write permission today), which avoids initiating pairing from our side. Test whether a bond forms at all on real hardware. If a system prompt appears, document it in the pairing procedure as an expected step rather than treating it as a fault.

risks.risk: Swift traps rather than throws on the three failure modes this driver's parsers depend on: array/Data out-of-range subscripting, integer overflow, and Double-to-Int conversion of NaN or infinity. Every path where Kotlin threw a catchable exception and degraded gracefully becomes an uncatchable process crash. A crash in a diabetes-monitoring app while the user is relying on it is materially worse than the rejected read the Android code produces.
risks.mitigation: Mandate explicit guard-based bounds checks returning typed errors in every parser, explicit widening or &-operators for all accumulation arithmetic, and an isFinite guard before every Double-to-Int conversion. Enforce all three with repo-authored static-analysis rules over the ble/read and ble/messages targets. Add fuzz/property tests feeding random and truncated byte arrays into every parse entry point and asserting a thrown error rather than a crash.

risks.risk: Data slices in Swift carry a non-zero startIndex. An index-based parser ported literally from Kotlin's zero-based ByteArray will silently read the wrong offsets after the first slicing operation, producing plausible-looking but wrong glucose, IOB and bolus values rather than failing.
risks.mitigation: Convert every incoming payload to [UInt8] at the transport boundary, or index exclusively via offsets relative to startIndex. Add a test that feeds each parser a payload embedded in a larger Data slice and asserts identical output to the zero-based case.

risks.risk: The pump drops idle connections at roughly 30 s and the driver depends on a 15 s poll as its keep-alive. iOS suspends the app between BLE events and gives roughly 10 s of runtime per wake; timers do not fire while suspended. A backgrounded iPhone may therefore drop the link and — because background advertising is not discoverable by name — fail to get it back.
risks.mitigation: Drive background operation from BLE events (disconnect, unsubscribe, notification arrival) rather than a wall clock, and design for the disconnect itself to be the wake source. Add a Live Activity so the app has a user-visible reason to be alive. Measure real background survival on Daniel's hardware over multi-hour sessions before claiming parity with Android's foreground service. Fall back to a time-sensitive notification prompting the user to open the app.

risks.risk: Swift actors do not guarantee FIFO ordering of awaiting continuations, whereas kotlinx.coroutines.Mutex is documented fair. A naive actor-based port of readMutex silently loses the property that keeps a 15 s glucose keep-alive from being starved by a multi-page history backfill — which in turn causes the pump's 30 s idle timeout to fire.
risks.mitigation: Implement an explicit FIFO async lock with an ordered continuation queue and unit-test its ordering under contention. Ban bare actors for the gateway's single-flight and history mutexes in the code-review checklist.

risks.risk: The SAKE session's per-direction sequence counters desync permanently if a late or duplicate notification is decrypted after an exchange has finished. Swift's cancellation semantics differ enough from kotlinx's that a literal port of the three guards (per-exchange finished flag, subscription watchdog, single-flight lock) may leave a gap — particularly because setNotifyValue(false) is asynchronous and a cancelled task's defer runs at an unpredictable point.
risks.mitigation: Drop notification handlers synchronously inside withTaskCancellationHandler before deferring any disable, keep the 30 s subscription watchdog as an independent backstop, and keep both identity guards (peripheral replaced by reconnect, characteristic re-subscribed by a newer exchange). Add a test that cancels an exchange mid-stream and asserts the next exchange decrypts correctly.

risks.risk: Semgrep's p/kotlin and p/java coverage does not transfer to Swift, so a literal tool-name port of the security gate would leave the iOS driver with materially less static analysis than the Android one, on the same safety-critical code.
risks.mitigation: Satisfy the requirement in substance: retain the language-agnostic p/secrets pack, add gitleaks, author a Swift rule set targeting this subsystem's actual invariants (write allow-list, isFinite-before-conversion, unchecked Data subscripting, PHI in warning-level logs), add Swift 6 strict concurrency as a hard gate, and wire MobSF as the advisory IPA-level analogue with the same documented revisit trigger. Keep the identical gate policy: fail on high/error only, fail closed on scanner crash.

risks.risk: TestFlight builds expire 90 days after upload, and internal testing requires each tester to be an App Store Connect user on the builder's own account. A user who builds once and forgets will silently lose their pump connection when the build expires.
risks.mitigation: Ship a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow in the fork template that rebuilds and re-uploads on a cadence comfortably inside 90 days, and document the expiry prominently in the fork-and-build guide. Note that internal-only distribution avoids Beta App Review entirely, so the rebuild is unattended.

risks.risk: CBCentral.identifier / CBPeripheral.identifier are not stable across app reinstall or after the user forgets the device in iOS Settings. A pairing record keyed on that UUID will appear valid while pointing at nothing, producing a paired-but-never-reconnects state that looks identical to a pump out of range.
risks.mitigation: Key durable identity on the pump's DIS serial number, read once after the first successful session, and treat the peer UUID as a cache. Distinguish 'paired, identifier not resolving' from 'paired, pump not in range' in the fault enum so the UI can offer re-pair rather than an indefinite wait.

risks.risk: CBPeripheralManager rejects an attempt to add a CCCD (0x2902) as a CBMutableDescriptor and raises an exception. A literal port of the Android GATT-server construction crashes at startup.
risks.mitigation: Delete all CCCD construction and the ungated descriptor-read workaround from the port; rely on didSubscribeTo / didUnsubscribeFrom. Cover this with a Simulator-runnable test that builds the local service tree (service construction does not require a powered radio) and asserts no descriptor is added to the SAKE characteristic.

risks.risk: The reverse-engineering document the Kotlin source cites by section throughout (Sec. 3 topology, 4-5 SAKE, 6 MTU, 7 single-peer, 8 GATT map, 9 E2E-CRC, 11 threading) is not in the Android repository. The iOS port would inherit citations pointing at nothing, and any protocol question that arises during hardware validation has no authoritative reference to consult.
risks.mitigation: Reconstruct the document from the Kotlin in-source comments as part of the port (they are complete enough to do so) and commit it to the iOS repo, so the Swift files cite something that exists. Do this before hardware validation, not after.

questions_for_pm: Is Medtronic 700-series support a blocking parity requirement for the iOS release, or an explicitly at-risk device? Two iOS-only unknowns — whether the pump will discover an iPhone that cannot advertise manufacturer-specific data, and whether Core Bluetooth can be made to open a client link back to the pump that just connected to us — can only be settled against a real 780G, and nobody on the team owns one (Daniel has a Tandem t:slim X2). If Medtronic must ship at parity, the project needs to fund or recruit a 780G tester before the driver architecture is committed; if it can ship as at-risk BETA behind a flag, the offline-provable majority can be built and validated in the Simulator now and the transport left unproven, matching the Android repo's existing posture.
